Web Tension Lines

New guides from modern-web-guidance, broken into problem lines: action, opponent, fallback, and what it unlocks. For ideas, read Unlock and the Idea box on the New capability lines. 754 lines (199 new capabilities), up to upstream v1.0.1. repo

Type
Outcome
Group by
One h1 per page so screen readers can find the main heading CorrectionWinN/A Accessibility coding guidelines · Semantic structure misrepresents the page
Action
Use a single <h1> for the page's main heading and <h2>–<h6> for the rest (a dialog's main heading is the exception)
Opponent
With several <h1> elements on a page, screen reader users can't tell which one is the main heading (quote: "Having more than one <h1> element on a page makes it difficult for screen reader users to identify the actual main heading.")
Fallback
Not needed — Heading levels use existing HTML semantics; the guide provides no browser support data

Screen reader users often jump to the h1 or scan the heading list to orient themselves, and multiple h1s break that entry point. The guide exempts h1s inside <dialog> / role="dialog", because a dialog is a separate window.

Support N/A (the guide has no browser support data at all)

mwg:accessibility · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

When a heading must toggle content, don't put it inside summary CorrectionWinN/A Accessibility coding guidelines · Inconsistent roles of native elements
Action
When a heading also acts as a disclosure trigger, use an ARIA accordion/disclosure where the heading wraps a button, not <details>/<summary>
Opponent
Some browsers expose <summary> as a button and strip all roles from its children, so the heading inside disappears (quote: "Some browsers still expose this element as a button, which removes all roles from its children including headings.")
Fallback
Not needed — This disclosure trigger pattern uses existing HTML and ARIA without new feature requirements

Same opponent as in the accordion and navbar guides: the summary role is implemented inconsistently. This general guide doesn't name a screen reader, only "some browsers".

Support N/A (the guide has no browser support data at all)

mwg:accessibility:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Use list markup only for real lists CorrectionWinN/A Accessibility coding guidelines · Over-announcing
Action
Use <ul>/<ol> only for repeated, contiguous items; don't wrap paragraphs in a list
Opponent
Marking separate paragraphs as a list makes screen readers announce list information, so users hear confusing and redundant content (quote: "screen readers will announce list information when they encounter lists, therefore leading to a screen reader hearing potentially confusing and redundant information about the related content.")
Fallback
Not needed — List markup uses existing HTML semantics without new feature requirements

List markup makes a screen reader say "list, N items" first, so misused lists become noise. The same section notes that checkboxes and radio buttons already announce their count, so wrapping them in a list duplicates it.

Support N/A (the guide has no browser support data at all)

mwg:accessibility:3 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Use CSS for layout and keep data tables navigable CorrectionWinN/A Accessibility coding guidelines · Semantic structure misrepresents the page
Action
Use Grid or Flexbox for layout and semantic, reasonably simple tables for data.
Opponent
Layout tables add redundant screen-reader structure and affect reading and focus order; complex tables disorient users. (quote: "Screen readers will announce redundant information about the layout, which may be confusing for screen reader users")
Fallback
Not needed — Table elements and layout use existing HTML/CSS without new feature requirements

Split tables when spanning, nesting, and expandable rows become difficult to navigate.

Support No support data; N/A.

mwg:accessibility:4 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Provide a small number of skip links for repeated content CorrectionWinN/A Accessibility coding guidelines · Hand-written focus management
Action
Add one or a few skip links with programmatically focusable targets only where repeated blocks warrant them.
Opponent
Missing links force repeated navigation, while too many links add frustrating Tab stops. (quote: "Multiple unnecessary skip links add to the number of Tab stops to a page, which causes frustration for people who use the keyboard alone for navigation.")
Fallback
Not needed — Skip links use existing HTML markup without new feature requirements

Skip targets and preceding important content need careful placement.

Support No support data; N/A.

mwg:accessibility:5 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Use native buttons instead of div role=button CorrectionWinN/A Accessibility coding guidelines · Hand-built controls lose native behavior
Action
Use button and required natively, adding ARIA only where HTML lacks the feature.
Opponent
A div with button role requires hand-built keyboard and activation behavior already supplied by native elements. (quote: "Native HTML elements and attributes already have the correct role and behavior, including keyboard support, built-in by default.")
Fallback
Not needed — Native elements and ARIA are existing mechanisms without new feature requirements

ARIA does not add behavior and should not duplicate native semantics.

Support No support data; N/A.

mwg:accessibility:6 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Do not override structural elements with interactive ARIA roles CorrectionWinN/A Accessibility coding guidelines · Semantic structure misrepresents the page
Action
Place button role on an inner span rather than the li itself.
Opponent
Interactive roles on structural elements destroy container semantics such as lists. (quote: "Use <li><span role="button">Button in a list</span></li>, not <li role="button">Button in a list</li>, to avoid breaking the container list semantics.")
Fallback
Not needed — Applying ARIA roles follows existing rules without new feature requirements

Structure and interaction should be expressed at separate levels.

Support No support data; N/A.

mwg:accessibility:7 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Use aria-disabled when users need to discover why a control is disabled CorrectionWinN/A Accessibility coding guidelines · Hiding or disabling locks people out
Action
Keep controls focusable with aria-disabled and block activation in JS; use disabled only when removing Tab access is intended.
Opponent
disabled removes elements from focus order entirely, preventing users from landing on them and learning their state. (quote: "disabled removes the element from the focus order entirely (and tabindex="0" won't bring it back)")
Fallback
Not needed — disabled and aria-disabled are existing attributes without new feature requirements

aria-disabled communicates state but does not prevent events by itself.

Support No support data; N/A.

mwg:accessibility:8 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Do not remove interactive semantics with presentation roles CorrectionWinN/A Accessibility coding guidelines · Semantic structure misrepresents the page
Action
Preserve native button and link roles instead of presentation or none.
Opponent
The element remains exposed but loses role and state, leaving users unable to understand its action. (quote: "The element will still be exposed to assistive technologies and announced by screen readers, but its role and any state information will not be")
Fallback
Not needed — role="presentation" is an existing ARIA role without new feature requirements

Presentation removes semantics rather than hiding the element.

Support No support data; N/A.

mwg:accessibility:9 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Associate labels explicitly with for and id CorrectionWinN/A Accessibility coding guidelines · Semantic structure misrepresents the page
Action
Match label for to the control id instead of relying only on nesting.
Opponent
Some voice-recognition tools require explicit for/id even when equivalent nesting is supported. (quote: "some assistive technologies, particularly voice recognition software, require the for/id relationship to be explicitly set")
Fallback
Not needed — for/id association uses existing HTML markup without new feature requirements

Visible proximity alone does not guarantee a programmatic relationship.

Support No support data; N/A.

mwg:accessibility:10 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Do not use title as a control accessible name CorrectionWinN/A Accessibility coding guidelines · Only reachable by hover
Action
Use labels, visible text, or appropriate ARIA instead of title, except for standard iframe naming.
Opponent
title appears only on mouse hover and cannot be accessed by keyboard. (quote: "The value of this attribute is only displayed on mouse hover, and cannot be displayed or otherwise accessed using the keyboard in any browser.")
Fallback
Not needed — title is an existing HTML attribute without new feature requirements

Keyboard focus does not reveal title-only explanations.

Support No support data; N/A.

mwg:accessibility:11 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Use placeholder only as a hint, not the label CorrectionWinN/A Accessibility coding guidelines · Semantic structure misrepresents the page
Action
Keep a visible label and use placeholder for examples or supplemental hints.
Opponent
Placeholder disappears during entry and its low contrast removes a persistent cue. (quote: "it disappears as soon as the user enters text into the field, meaning that there is no longer a visual cue as to what the field represents.")
Fallback
Not needed — placeholder and <label> use existing HTML markup without new feature requirements

Users should not have to infer a field from their own input.

Support No support data; N/A.

mwg:accessibility:12 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Disambiguate identical Edit buttons in their accessible names CorrectionWinN/A Accessibility coding guidelines · Semantic structure misrepresents the page
Action
Add visually hidden text, aria-label, or aria-labelledby to identify each edit target while retaining visible Edit text.
Opponent
Screen readers hear only a series of identical Edit buttons without their targets. (quote: "screen reader users may only hear "Edit, button".")
Fallback
Not needed — Accessible naming uses existing ARIA attributes without new feature requirements

Visual context is not always included in the accessible name.

Support No support data; N/A.

mwg:accessibility:13 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Keep labels concise and move descriptions and repeated state out CorrectionWinN/A Accessibility coding guidelines · Over-announcing
Action
Use aria-describedby for supplemental content and avoid repeating ARIA state or role in labels.
Opponent
Verbose labels frustrate users and duplicated state or role produces redundant announcements. (quote: "Verbose labels confuse and frustrate people who use screen readers.")
Fallback
Not needed — aria-describedby is an existing ARIA attribute without new feature requirements

Required, expanded, and checked states belong to native or ARIA attributes.

Support No support data; N/A.

mwg:accessibility:14 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Mark page and inline language changes with lang CorrectionWinN/A Accessibility coding guidelines · Semantic structure misrepresents the page
Action
Set the main language on html and the correct lang on containers for foreign passages.
Opponent
Mismatched lang makes screen readers and text-to-speech output unintelligible. (quote: "This causes screen readers and other text-to-speech software to announce the content in a non-understandable manner.")
Fallback
Not needed — lang is an existing HTML attribute without new feature requirements

A foreign sentence needs local metadata, not a page-wide language change.

Support No support data; N/A.

mwg:accessibility:15 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Give every page a unique front-loaded title and update it in SPAs CorrectionWinN/A Accessibility coding guidelines · Semantic structure misrepresents the page
Action
Use Page Topic | Site Name, avoid duplicates, and update title on route and completion changes.
Opponent
Empty, duplicate, or vague titles make pages indistinguishable without reading their content. (quote: "In such cases, pages are indistinguishable without reviewing the actual page content itself.")
Fallback
Not needed — <title> is an existing HTML element without new feature requirements

SPA titles must follow application state rather than remain on the previous view.

Support No support data; N/A.

mwg:accessibility:16 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Keep iframe scrolling available for zoomed content CorrectionWinN/A Accessibility coding guidelines · Hiding or disabling locks people out
Action
Avoid scrolling=no and overflow:hidden and provide a descriptive iframe title.
Opponent
Users who zoom need scrolling to reach overflowing iframe content. (quote: "Users who zoom in or enlarge text need to scroll to reach content that overflows.")
Fallback
Not needed — Iframe scrolling is existing behavior without new feature requirements

Embedded content must not be clipped for visual neatness.

Support No support data; N/A.

mwg:accessibility:17 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Avoid positive tabindex and let DOM determine focus order CorrectionWinN/A Accessibility coding guidelines · Hand-written focus management
Action
Remove positive tabindex, avoid redundant tabindex=0 on native controls, and keep static or hidden content out of Tab.
Opponent
Positive tabindex imposes a sequence unrelated to the intended page order. (quote: "doing so imposes a tab order on the page that bears no resemblance to the intended or expected tab order.")
Fallback
Not needed — tabindex is an existing HTML attribute without new feature requirements

Promoting one control with positive tabindex disrupts the entire page sequence.

Support No support data; N/A.

mwg:accessibility:18 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Avoid touch-action:none for custom gestures CorrectionWinN/A Accessibility coding guidelines · Native scroll gestures don't fit the use
Action
Restrict only the required axis with pan-x or pan-y, reserving none for surfaces such as drawing canvases.
Opponent
touch-action:none disables page scrolling through the element. (quote: "This disables page scrolling through the element.")
Fallback
Not needed — touch-action is an existing CSS property without new feature requirements

Horizontal swiping should not disable vertical page scrolling.

Support No support data; N/A.

mwg:accessibility:19 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Provide or suppress image and SVG alternatives according to purpose CorrectionWinN/A Accessibility coding guidelines · Duplicate content confuses assistive tech
Action
Use meaningful alt or SVG names for informative visuals and empty alt or aria-hidden for decorative ones.
Opponent
Missing alternatives lose meaning, while exposed decorative visuals create irrelevant announcements. (quote: "Do apply alt="" to decorative visuals: This prevents screen readers from announcing them.")
Fallback
Not needed — alt and ARIA image roles are existing mechanisms without new feature requirements

Describe function such as Search rather than appearance such as magnifying glass.

Support No support data; N/A.

mwg:accessibility:20 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Centralize and coordinate live-region announcements CorrectionWinN/A Accessibility coding guidelines · Announcements mistimed or unreliable
Action
Use one polite and one assertive region, debounce frequent updates, and coordinate messages with inert state.
Opponent
Noisy regions spam users, while messages in inert DOM may be missed or announced from unreachable content. (quote: "queued or debounced messages will be unannounced — or announced from DOM the user can't reach.")
Fallback
Not needed — Live regions and inert are existing ARIA/HTML mechanisms without new feature requirements

Use progress for busy states and assertive only for critical interruptions.

Support No support data; N/A.

mwg:accessibility:21 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Use dialog.showModal() for modals and inert only for custom overlays CorrectionWinN/A Accessibility coding guidelines · Hand-written focus management
Action
Use native modal dialog; otherwise make outside content inert, assign dialog role, and move focus into the overlay.
Opponent
The guide calls hand-written traps and overlay management error-prone without a concrete failure. (quote: "all of which are error prone and require heavy JavaScript event tracking to maintain.")
Fallback
Not needed — Native <dialog> is an existing HTML element without new feature requirements
Unlock
Previously modals required hand-rolling focus traps, inert, top-layering, and backdrops; now native <dialog>'s .showModal() handles all of it at once

A custom overlay must not sit inside its own inert ancestor.

Support No support data; N/A.

mwg:accessibility:22 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Sync aria-invalid with :user-invalid so errors aren't announced before input CorrectionWinWidely Accessible error announcement · Announcements mistimed or unreliable
Action
Show errors with :user-invalid, and use a small script on blur/change/input/invalid to check it and set aria-invalid to match; until then, set aria-invalid="false" explicitly
Opponent
With :invalid alone, a screen reader says "Invalid entry" as soon as the user tabs into an empty required field, before any interaction (quote: "screen readers might announce \"Invalid entry\" the moment a user tabs into a required field that is currently empty.")
Fallback
Not needed — :user-invalid is already Widely available (since 2023-11-02); no fallback needed

:user-invalid only affects the visuals; it doesn't touch ARIA. The guide also points out that Firefox and Safari expose an empty required field as invalid from page load, so aria-invalid can't be left unset and must be false. You still write the bridging script yourself, because there is no "UserInvalidChanged" event.

Support :user-valid / :user-invalid: Widely (2023-11-02)

mwg:accessible-error-announcement · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Reference the error from aria-describedby only while it's shown CorrectionWinWidely Accessible error announcement · Announcements mistimed or unreliable
Action
Point the field at its error message with data-error, and let the script add that id to aria-describedby only while the field is invalid
Opponent
Referencing the error from aria-describedby in the markup means it is read even while hidden, so users hear the error before interacting (quote: "text that aria-describedby references is announced even when it's hidden, so the error would be read out before the user has interacted.")
Fallback
Not needed — aria-describedby is an existing ARIA attribute; no browser support data in the guide

The error element is always in the page, just hidden with display: none, so leaving the reference in place feels harmless. But aria-describedby ignores visibility, so the reference itself has to follow the state.

Support :user-valid / :user-invalid: Widely (2023-11-02); no support data given for aria-describedby

mwg:accessible-error-announcement:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Announce errors through one shared polite live region, not a live region per error CorrectionWinWidely Accessible error announcement · Announcements mistimed or unreliable
Action
Put one aria-live="polite" region on the page and write "label: error" into it about 500ms after a field is left or changed; after a failed submit, move focus to the first invalid field
Opponent
Making each error message its own live region fails because it is shown rather than changed, so screen readers don't announce it reliably (quote: "a live region that is shown, rather than changed, isn't announced reliably.")
Fallback
Not needed — Live regions are an existing ARIA mechanism; no browser support data in the guide

A common pattern is putting aria-live on each error <span> and toggling its display, which announces only some of the time. The guide uses a single announcer that receives text instead. When the field is fixed, the announcer is also cleared so the old error isn't found later while reading the page.

Support :user-valid / :user-invalid: Widely (2023-11-02); no support data given for live regions

mwg:accessible-error-announcement:3 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Silence decorative glyphs with content's alt-text argument New capabilityPartialNewly Accessible CSS generated content · Over-announcing
Idea · brainstormArrows, separators and status icons inserted with CSS can be declared silent, or given a spoken label, right in the stylesheet, without wrapping each icon in an extra aria-hidden span. An icon system can live entirely in CSS without adding screen reader noise.
Action
Add alt text to content after a /: content: " →" / ""; for decoration, content: url(icon.svg) / "Save"; for a meaningful icon
Opponent
Without the / syntax, decorative glyphs inserted with ::after are read out by screen readers (quote: "Fallback: render the glyph in browsers without / support (screen readers there will still announce it)")
Fallback
Loses the main benefit — Falling back to single-value content still renders symbols, but screen readers read them again and noise returns
Unlock
Previously CSS-generated content could not specify screen-reader output; now content alt text declares what meaningful icons say and silences decorative ones

CSS-added arrows and separator dots turn into noise like "right arrow" in a screen reader. The new syntax lets CSS itself declare "don't read this" or "read it as this". The guide stresses this is harm reduction: meaningful text still belongs in the DOM.

Support Alt text for generated content: Newly (2024-07-09; Chrome 77, Edge 79, Firefox 128, Safari 17.4)

mwg:accessible-generated-content · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Don't repeat text already in the DOM as content alt text CorrectionPartialNewly Accessible CSS generated content · Over-announcing
Action
Use the alt-text argument only when the text differs from the primary value and isn't already in the DOM
Opponent
A button labelled "Save" with / "Save" on its ::before icon is read as "Save save" (quote: "A screen reader would read it out as \"Save save\".")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — Falling back to single-value content still displays the icon without alt text, avoiding duplicate announcements with button labels

The new syntax invites the idea that every icon needs alt text, which then stacks on top of the button's own label. The guide also says images are presentational by default, so don't add empty alt text, and emoji alt text is only for when it differs from the official name.

Support Alt text for generated content: Newly (2024-07-09)

mwg:accessible-generated-content:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Use meta text-scale so the page follows the system font size New capabilityStalemateLimited Respecting the OS text scale · User settings get ignored
Idea · brainstormWeb pages can follow the phone's system font size (Dynamic Type) like native apps, so older or low-vision users don't have to adjust every site. Reading and documentation pages benefit most; Chrome/Edge 146+ only for now.
Action
Put <meta name="text-scale" content="scale"> in <head>, size text and spacing in rem/em, and use unitless line heights
Opponent
Users set a larger system font size on iOS/Android, but mobile browsers ignore it by default and the page text stays the same (quote: "By default, mobile browsers ignore these OS-level accessibility settings to prevent legacy, fixed-pixel websites from breaking visually.")
Fallback
Loses the main benefit — Unsupported browsers fall back to default text sizing, still ignoring OS font-size preferences unless users zoom manually
Unlock
Previously mobile browsers ignored OS text scale to protect legacy sites; now a meta tag opts in so the browser applies the OS ratio to the root font size

Browsers ignore the system font size to protect old fixed-px sites. The meta tag is the page declaring "my layout can take it", and only then is the system scale applied to 1rem. After opting in you must not set font-size on :root yourself, nor multiply by env(preferred-text-scale) again, or scaling is blocked or doubled.

Support <meta name="text-scale">: Limited (Chrome 146, Edge 146; not Firefox or Safari)

mwg:respect-os-text-scale · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Fluid font sizes need a rem component, not vw alone CorrectionWinWidely Respecting the OS text scale · User settings get ignored
Action
Write fluid font sizes like clamp(2rem, 1.25rem + 2vw, 4rem) so they have both a font-relative and a viewport-relative part
Opponent
With font-size: 5vw alone, text doesn't fully respond to the user's text scaling (quote: "The font size does not respond fully to user text scaling")
Fallback
Not needed — clamp() and rem are already Widely available; no fallback needed

Pure vw sizes follow only the viewport width, so when the user enlarges text the headings don't move. The guide adds rules of thumb: keep the maximum no more than 2.5 times the minimum, and test 200% text resize and reflow at 320 CSS px wide.

Support — (the guide gives support data only for meta text-scale, not for clamp()/rem)

mwg:respect-os-text-scale:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

With text-scale on, don't hard-code font-size on html CorrectionStalemateLimited Respecting the OS text scale · User settings get ignored
Action
Leave the root font size to the browser: no font-size on :root/html, whether absolute, relative or calculated
Opponent
Writing font-size: 16px on html can stop the browser from applying text scaling (quote: "This can prevent the browser from applying text scaling")
Fallback
Loses the main benefit — Fall back to the default font size and manual scaling, so the root font size still doesn't follow the system preference

Many resets and design systems pin 16px on html as a baseline, and that one line cancels the opt-in. The guide lists it as a DO NOT, and separately warns against combining it with env(preferred-text-scale), which scales twice.

Support <meta name="text-scale">: Limited (Chrome 146, Edge 146)

mwg:respect-os-text-scale:3 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Detect text language in the browser with LanguageDetector New capabilityStalemateLimited Language detection · Must send to the cloud or load a big library
Idea · brainstormPasted text can have its language detected on-device and get the right lang automatically on comments or note paragraphs, so screen readers pronounce it correctly, without sending the content to a server. Chrome/Edge desktop only for now, with hardware requirements.
Action
Check with LanguageDetector.availability(), create the detector from a user gesture with LanguageDetector.create(), and get a confidence-ranked language list from detect()
Opponent
(missing) The guide only says it reduces the need for heavy external libraries or costly server calls, without saying where the old approach fails (quote: "it enhances user privacy and reduces the need for heavy external libraries or costly server-side calls.")
Fallback
Loses the main benefit — Falling back to cloud APIs or disabling the feature sends content off-device again, bringing back privacy and cost issues
Unlock
Previously detecting language required cloud APIs or heavy libraries; now the browser detects it on-device without sending data to Google or third parties

Uses include detecting the source language before translation and setting the right lang on content. The guide stresses detection runs locally and sends nothing to Google or third parties, but never describes a concrete failure of the old way. The model download needs a user gesture, 22 GB of storage and 16 GB of RAM, and accuracy drops sharply on very short phrases.

Support Language detector: Limited (Chrome 138, Edge 148; not Firefox or Safari)

mwg:language-detection · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Run Gemini Nano in the browser with the Prompt API New capabilityPartialLimited Language model (Prompt API) · Must send to the cloud or load a big library
Idea · brainstormClassify, rewrite or answer questions about images inside the page without a server, for example a notes app tagging each diary entry on-device or turning screenshots into text. Data stays on the device and it works offline. Chrome 148 desktop only for now, with hardware requirements.
Action
Check with LanguageModel.availability(), download the model from a user gesture via LanguageModel.create(), then handle text, image and audio input with prompt()/promptStreaming()
Opponent
(missing) The guide only lists the benefits of running locally (privacy, lower server cost, offline), without saying where the old approach fails (quote: "This built-in AI approach ensures user privacy, reduces server costs, and enables offline functionality.")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — Fall back to a cloud API or Transformers.js, losing the convenience of built-in model deployment
Unlock
Previously browser inference meant loading your own model or calling the cloud; now LanguageModel runs on-device with text, image, and audio input, even offline

The guide covers session management (clone(), initialPrompts, destroy()), multimodal input and JSON Schema structured output. The opponent appears only as the flip side of the benefits, with no observable failure. Hardware requirements are high (22 GB storage, 16 GB RAM), and the download needs a user gesture plus visible progress.

Support LanguageModel: Limited (Chrome 148; not Edge, Firefox or Safari)

mwg:language-model · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Always write model output with textContent, never innerHTML CorrectionWinWidely Language model (Prompt API) · Untrusted content parsed as HTML
Action
Write model responses into textContent; when limited HTML is needed, run the Sanitizer API or DOMPurify over the **complete** output
Opponent
Model output is untrusted and can contain injected markup, so setting innerHTML directly becomes XSS (quote: "Model output is untrusted and can contain injected markup. Always use textContent or a sanitizer.")
Fallback
Not needed — textContent and sanitizers are existing mechanisms; no fallback needed

The usual streaming pattern is innerHTML += for each chunk. The guide says that is slow and injectable, and malicious code can be split across two chunks, so sanitize the combined output, not each chunk.

Support — (no support data given for textContent)

mwg:language-model:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Set aria-busy while streaming so screen readers read the full response, not each chunk CorrectionWinWidely Language model (Prompt API) · Over-announcing
Action
Make the output container a polite live region present from page load, set aria-busy="true" while streaming and false after; don't move focus during streaming
Opponent
Without aria-busy, the live region reads out every streamed chunk (quote: "so assistive technologies announce the complete response rather than each chunk")
Fallback
Not needed — aria-busy and live regions are existing ARIA mechanisms; no fallback needed

The typewriter effect is feedback for sighted users and broken fragments for screen reader users. When the output language differs from the page, the output element must also get lang so it is pronounced correctly.

Support — (no support data given for aria-busy / live regions)

mwg:language-model:3 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Call create() from a user gesture when model download is required CorrectionPartialLimited Language model (Prompt API) · Permission requests fired out of context
Action
Call LanguageModel.create() inside a button or other user event when availability requires downloading.
Opponent
Calling create() on page load for a download rejects with NotAllowedError. (quote: "Call it from an event listener, not on page load, or it rejects with a NotAllowedError.")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — Fall back to a cloud or alternative local model, no longer triggering the built-in model download gesture error

Check availability first and require explicit activation for downloads.

Support LanguageModel: Limited; Chrome 148 only.

mwg:language-model:4 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Show accessible model download progress and completion CorrectionStalemateLimited Language model (Prompt API) · Focus or state indicators disappear
Action
Use a named progress element for downloadprogress and a polite live region for completion, not only the console.
Opponent
A large model download without visible progress makes the UI appear frozen. (quote: "Inform the user while the model downloads so the UI doesn't appear frozen.")
Fallback
Loses the main benefit — With cloud API fallback there is no local model to download, so download progress tracking is inapplicable

A 22 GB download needs visible and audible status.

Support LanguageModel: Limited; Chrome 148 only.

mwg:language-model:5 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Move focus before hiding download or stop controls CorrectionStalemateLimited Language model (Prompt API) · Hand-written focus management
Action
Move focus to status text or the initiating control before hiding the currently focused button.
Opponent
Hiding the focused button leaves keyboard users without a location. (quote: "If the button that starts the download is hidden while it has focus, move focus to the download's status text")
Fallback
Not stated — The guide doesn't say what to do without support

Button-state changes must include focus management.

Support LanguageModel: Limited; Chrome 148 only.

mwg:language-model:6 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Set lang on model output when its language differs CorrectionPartialLimited Language model (Prompt API) · Semantic structure misrepresents the page
Action

A "show more" section or a dismissible alert growing from 0 to its content height used to need JS measuring or max-height hacks. :not() only asks whether some ancestor matches, not which one is nearest, so it goes wrong once components nest. The lower bound of @scope makes exclusion follow the nearest scope root. The same guide uses @scope to fix .dark .invert / .light .invert always resolving to one theme when nested.

* { box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0 } is almost a reflex, but it hits every element, including parts of web components that want to decide for themselves. The guide advocates managing priority with @layer and :where(), which a global reset works against.

mwg:autofill-address-form:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Validate names and addresses with Unicode letter matching, not Latin-only CorrectionWinN/A Building an address form that follows best practice · Forms assume the wrong data shape
Action
Use Unicode letter matching (e.g. \p{L}) in validation regexes and make sure the backend handles Unicode input and output securely
Opponent
Latin-only regexes shut out users whose names or addresses contain non-Latin characters (quote: "Latin-only excludes users with names or addresses that include characters that aren't in the Latin alphabet.")
Fallback
Not needed — Unicode letter regex matching is supported across modern browsers; no fallback needed

[A-Za-z]+ looks like a sensible name check, but names like 王小明 or Олег fail it, so the form rejects real names. A Unicode letter class lets the same rule cover every script.

Support N/A (the guide only says "Unicode in regular expressions is well supported by modern browsers." with no Baseline data)

mwg:autofill-address-form:3 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Add a non-color indicator with :autofill instead of relying on the browser tint CorrectionStalemateLimited Styling autofilled form fields · Focus or state indicators disappear
Action
Give input:autofill at least one indicator that isn't color, such as a thicker inset ring box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px …
Opponent
The browser's default autofill highlight is color only (quote: "The browser's default highlight is color only.")
Fallback
Loses the main benefit — Fall back to the default background or :-webkit-autofill, while ordinary Firefox fields still only get a color

Users who can't tell the tint apart can't see which fields the browser filled. An inset ring makes it visible by shape too. Firefox's other fields have no workaround, and the guide explicitly says not to add a JavaScript fallback.

Support :autofill: Limited (Chrome 110, Edge 110, Safari 15; not Firefox)

mwg:autofill-highlight-inputs · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

If autofill styling uses outline, make the focus outline differ in more than color CorrectionPartialLimited Styling autofilled form fields · Focus or state indicators disappear
Action
Don't remove the focus outline; if the autofill style itself uses outline, give :autofill:focus-visible an outline that differs in thickness, style or offset
Opponent
When autofill and focus both use outlines that differ only in color, you can't tell which field has focus (quote: "give :autofill:focus-visible an outline that differs in more than color (e.g. thickness, style, or offset) so focus remains perceivable.")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — Falls back to browser default styling; focus remains visible, only autofill vs. focus distinction relies on color

A whole column of fields gets autofilled with the same outline, and as a keyboard user tabs through, the focused one differs only slightly in color, which is as good as no focus ring. Making focus differ in thickness or offset keeps it distinguishable.

Support :autofill: Limited

mwg:autofill-highlight-inputs:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Don't change border-width or padding in autofill styles CorrectionPartialLimited Styling autofilled form fields · Layout unexpectedly overflows or shifts
Action
In :autofill only change properties that don't affect layout (inset shadows, border color), not border-width or padding
Opponent
The autofill state toggles with user activity, so layout-affecting properties make content shift (quote: "the state toggles with user activity so that would shift content.")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — Falls back to browser default styling with no autofill-induced layout shift anyway

The user picks an autofill suggestion, borders thicken and the form pushes down; they edit a field, the state clears and it shrinks back. An inset shadow is just as visible without changing geometry.

Support :autofill: Limited

mwg:autofill-highlight-inputs:3 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Preserve focus shadows and caret color when overriding autofill colors CorrectionPartialLimited Styling autofilled form fields · Focus or state indicators disappear
Action
Prefer the browser colors; otherwise use inset shadow, -webkit-text-fill-color, and caret-color, repeating existing focus shadows in the same declaration.
Opponent
UA !important colors require workarounds, and an inset-shadow workaround replaces existing box-shadow focus rings. (quote: "All browsers also set background-color, background-image, and color on autofilled fields with !important in their user agent stylesheets, so overriding them relies on workarounds.")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — Unsupported browsers keep their default background; autofill still works, just without custom colors

The brand background and focus ring compete for the same box-shadow property.

Support :autofill: Limited.

mwg:autofill-highlight-inputs:4 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Give payment fields cc-* autocomplete tokens and prefix billing address fields CorrectionWinWidely Building a payment form that follows best practice · Autofill fails
Action
Use autocomplete="cc-number", cc-name, cc-exp and cc-csc for card fields; default billing to the delivery address and distinguish sections with shipping/billing prefixes (e.g. billing address-line1)
Opponent
Without autocomplete, users may write card details down or store them insecurely (quote: "Without autocomplete, users may keep a physical record of payment card details or store them insecurely.")
Fallback
Not needed — autocomplete is already Widely available; nothing needs a fallback

Every checkout means pulling out the card and copying sixteen digits, so some people just keep the number in a notes file. With proper tokens the browser keeps and fills it; prefixes keep shipping and billing addresses from filling into each other.

Support No autocomplete support data in this guide (Widely 2015-07-29 per autofill-address-form); enterkeyhint, Email/telephone/URL input types and inputmode are Widely

mwg:autofill-payment-form · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Use a single name field with autocomplete="name" where possible CorrectionWinWidely Building a payment form that follows best practice · Forms assume the wrong data shape
Action
Unless you really need to store given name, family name or honorifics separately, use one name field with autocomplete="name"
Opponent
(missing) The guide only lists benefits of a single field, without directly saying when split fields fail (quote: "Using a single name input makes forms less complex, enables cut-and-paste, and makes autofill simpler.")
Fallback
Not needed — autocomplete is Widely available; how fields are split is entirely your choice

This section is word-for-word the same as in the address form guide. The cardholder name has its own cc-name, and the guide's example also collects it in one field.

Support No autocomplete support data in this guide (Widely 2015-07-29 per autofill-address-form)

mwg:autofill-payment-form:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Use Unicode letter matching in validation regexes, e.g. pattern="[\p{L} \-\.]+" on the cardholder field, and make sure the backend handles Unicode securely
Opponent
Latin-only regexes shut out users whose names or addresses contain non-Latin characters (quote: "Latin-only excludes users with names or addresses that include characters that aren't in the Latin alphabet.")
Fallback
Not needed — Unicode letter regex matching is supported across modern browsers; no fallback needed

This section is word-for-word the same as in the address form guide. On a payment page, rejecting a name costs a lost order.

mwg:autofill-payment-form:3 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Use text and numeric inputmode for card numbers CorrectionWinWidely Building a payment form that follows best practice · Wrong native control for the job
Action
Use type="text", inputmode="numeric", and cc-number autocomplete, allowing spaces and appropriate lengths.
Opponent
Number inputs add spinners and strip leading zeros. (quote: "DO NOT use type="number" — it adds increment/decrement controls and strips leading zeros")
Fallback
Not needed — inputmode is already Widely available; numeric keyboards have no fallback issue

A card number is an identifier, not a quantity.

Support inputmode: Widely.

mwg:autofill-payment-form:4 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Place payment format hints above the input CorrectionWinN/A Building a payment form that follows best practice · Popovers cover instructions
Action
Put persistent hints above fields and connect them with aria-describedby; use placeholder only as an extra cue.
Opponent
Mobile keyboards and autofill popovers cover hints below inputs, and placeholder disappears during entry. (quote: "Hints that sit below an input are easily hidden by the mobile keyboard or by the autofill popover at the moment the user needs them.")
Fallback
Not needed — Pure layout arrangement; does not depend on browser feature support

Moving the hint avoids both overlays.

Support Layout placement; N/A.

mwg:autofill-payment-form:5 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Do not mask the card security code CorrectionWinWidely Building a payment form that follows best practice · Forms assume the wrong data shape
Action
Use type="text", numeric inputmode, and cc-csc autocomplete instead of type="password".
Opponent
Users cannot check masked digits, so a typo appears only after payment is declined. (quote: "Users can't check a masked three- or four-digit code for typos, so a mistyped digit isn't caught until the payment is declined")
Fallback
Not needed — inputmode is Widely available; masking choices are up to the form

Masking a code printed on the card adds little protection but removes a useful check.

Support inputmode: Widely.

mwg:autofill-payment-form:6 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Use one field for card and phone numbers CorrectionWinN/A Building a payment form that follows best practice · Autofill fails
Action
Keep each number in one input and create grouped visuals with styling rather than multiple fields.
Opponent
Splitting numbers prevents browser autofill and complicates entry and validation. (quote: "For payment card and phone numbers use a single input: don't split the number into parts. That makes it easier for users to enter data, makes validation simpler, and enables browsers to autofill.")
Fallback
Not needed — Single field vs. split boxes is a form markup choice, not a browser support issue

The visual grouping no longer determines the data-entry structure.

Support No support data; N/A.

mwg:autofill-payment-form:7 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Allow varied card lengths and spaces in patterns CorrectionWinN/A Building a payment form that follows best practice · Forms assume the wrong data shape
Action
Accept valid issuer lengths and spaces, removing spaces before processing.
Opponent
Rigid patterns reject valid cards and the grouped spaces printed on physical cards. (quote: "Allow users to include spaces when they're entering a new payment card number, since this is how numbers are displayed on physical cards.")
Fallback
Not needed — Validation rules belong to the backend and form logic, not browser feature support

Users should not have to retype the format shown on their card.

Support Regular-expression validation; N/A.

mwg:autofill-payment-form:8 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Use username/current-password so password managers can save and fill sign-in fields CorrectionWinWidely Building a sign-in form that follows best practice · Autofill fails
Action
Use autocomplete="username" on the email field and autocomplete="current-password" on the password field; keep name/id stable, not random, inside a <form> with a submit button
Opponent
Without autocomplete, users are more likely to write sign-in details down or store them insecurely on their device; with randomly generated name/id values or no <form>, browsers won't store the data (quote: "Without autocomplete, users may be more likely to keep a physical record of sign-in details, or store sign-in data insecurely on their device.")
Fallback
Not needed — autocomplete is already Widely available; nothing needs a fallback

The password manager has the credentials, yet the sign-in page shows no suggestion, maybe because field names change with every deploy or the 'form' is just a pile of <div>s. Clear roles and stable names connect saving and filling.

Support No autocomplete support data in this guide (Widely 2015-07-29 per autofill-address-form); Email/telephone/URL input types and inputmode are Widely

mwg:autofill-sign-in-form · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Turn off spellcheck and autocorrect on username and email fields CorrectionPartialNewly Building a sign-in form that follows best practice · Forms assume the wrong data shape
Action
Add spellcheck="false" to username and email fields; also turn off autocorrect and autocapitalize on non-email usernames (type="email" already disables them)
Opponent
Usernames are identifiers, not prose, and the browser can 'correct' them into something the account doesn't match (quote: "Add spellcheck="false" so the browser does not rewrite them into something the account does not match.")
Fallback
Not stated — The guide doesn't say what to do when autocorrect is unsupported

Spellcheck, autocorrect and autocapitalize are designed for prose; applied to a username, the submitted string no longer matches the account. Turn them off on identifier fields and leave the defaults on free-text fields like messages and comments.

Support autocorrect: Newly (2026-09-11); no support data for spellcheck or autocapitalize in this guide

mwg:autofill-sign-in-form:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Support Layout placement; N/A.

Sign-up is the moment the browser learns the credentials; if field roles are unclear, the user has to remember them for every later sign-in. Marking new-password is what makes the browser offer and save a generated strong password.
