mwg:autofill-sign-up-form:8 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Rebrand checkboxes and radios with one line of accent-color instead of rebuilding them New capabilityStalemateLimited Brand-consistent forms · Hand-built controls lose native behavior
Idea · brainstormBrand-colored checkboxes, sliders and progress bars used to mean rewriting the controls → surveys and settings pages can use native controls recolored with one line of CSS, with indeterminate, keyboard and focus handled by the browser. Only affects checkbox, radio, range and progress
Action
Set accent-color: var(--brand-color) on body or a form container so checkbox, radio, range and progress take the brand color; pair it with color-scheme for dark mode
Opponent
Building custom controls from scratch takes time and easily leads to accessibility issues or missing states such as a checkbox's indeterminate state (quote: "Building custom controls is time-consuming and can easily lead to accessibility issues or missing states (like the indeterminate state for checkboxes).")
Fallback
Loses the main benefit — Falling back to visually hiding native inputs and redrawing checkboxes/sliders loses the one-line brand tint that keeps native states intact
Unlock
Previously native checkboxes were locked to browser colors unless rebuilt custom; one line of accent-color applies brand colors to native controls

The design calls for brand-purple checkboxes, native controls only come in the browser's default blue, so the usual fix was hiding the native input and redrawing it with pseudo-elements, often forgetting indeterminate or focus styles. accent-color recolors the native controls themselves. The guide still requires keeping the redraw for unsupported browsers.

Support accent-color: Limited per the guide (which also lists Chrome 93, Edge 93, Firefox 92 and Safari 26.2 as supporting; marked Limited despite all four, pending manual check)

mwg:brand-consistent-forms · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Pick an accent-color with enough contrast yourself instead of trusting automatic inversion CorrectionPartialLimited Brand-consistent forms · Focus or state indicators disappear
Action
Choose a brand color with at least 3:1 contrast against the background, use a lighter value in dark mode, and pair it with color-scheme: light dark
Opponent
Safari (WebKit bug 244233) and Android Chrome (Chromium bug 343503163) can fail to invert the checkmark color, leaving controls invisible or hard to see when contrast is low (quote: "can fail to invert checkmark colors, leading to invisible or hard-to-see controls when using colors that lack sufficient contrast against the background")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — Unsupported browsers fall back to default browser appearance; controls stay visible, just without brand tint

A pale yellow brand color in light mode should, in theory, get an automatically contrasting checkmark, but some implementations don't, and checked versus unchecked becomes nearly invisible. The guide's answer: don't bet on the browser, pick a contrasting color from the start.

Support accent-color: Limited (as above; the guide's status is questionable)

mwg:brand-consistent-forms:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Build branded dropdowns with appearance: base-select instead of rebuilding them in JS New capabilityPartialLimited Branded select styling · Hand-built controls lose native behavior
Idea · brainstormA branded dropdown used to mean writing your own listbox component → every dropdown in a form can match the design system in pure CSS, with keyboard, screen reader and submission needing no extra work. Firefox falls back to the system menu
Action
Set appearance: base-select on <select> and ::picker(select), use a <button> containing <selectedcontent> as the trigger, and style the list, arrow and checkmark via ::picker(select), ::picker-icon and option::checkmark
Opponent
A fully branded dropdown used to require rebuilding the control from scratch in JavaScript, which often broke accessibility, keyboard navigation and native form integration (quote: "Previously, achieving a fully branded select required rebuilding the control from scratch with JavaScript, which often broke accessibility, keyboard navigation, and native form integration.")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — Falls back to the OS dropdown menu, keeping selection and form submission working just without brand styling
Unlock
Previously branded dropdowns had to be rebuilt in JS; base-select lets CSS style the appearance while keeping native behavior

The design system wants dropdowns with dashed borders and monospace type like every other control; native <select> couldn't do it, so teams built their own and then had to re-add arrow keys, screen reader support and form submission one by one. base-select puts the look entirely in CSS while behavior stays native. The cost: no native iOS wheel picker.

Support Customizable <select>: Limited (Chrome 135, Edge 135, Safari 27; not Firefox)

mwg:branded-select-styling · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Lay out the native select picker as a grid of cards with base-select and grid New capabilityPartialLimited Custom select picker layouts · Hand-built controls lose native behavior
Idea · brainstormOptions used to be a column of text, and visual choices meant writing your own component → colors, sizes, stickers or plan comparisons can be a native <select> laid out as a card grid that submits with the form. Firefox falls back to text only; Left/Right navigation and grid semantics for screen readers remain limited
Action
Set appearance: base-select on <select> and ::picker(select), use display: grid on select:open::picker(select), put images or SVGs in <option> as cards, and mark the chosen one with option:checked and ::checkmark
Opponent
(missing) The guide only says you can break away from the traditional vertical list without custom JS, without saying when the list or custom JS goes wrong (quote: "break away from the traditional stacked vertical list and create a rich visual experience without custom JS.")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — Falls back to the OS dropdown menu, keeping selection and form submission working, just arranged vertically
Unlock
Previously native selects could only stack options vertically; the picker can arrange options in a CSS grid as cards with native behavior

Color swatches, emoji or product variants are easier to choose from a grid than a long text list, which used to mean abandoning <select> and building your own. The picker can now use grid layout while value and submission stay native. But native select only handles Up/Down, so a grid layout needs extra keyboard handling.

Support Customizable <select>: Limited (Chrome 135, Edge 135, Safari 27; not Firefox)

mwg:custom-select-picker-layouts · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Put picker layout styles only on :open CorrectionPartialLimited Custom select picker layouts · Hidden preconditions of new features
Action
Write layout styles like display: grid on select:open::picker(select), not directly on select::picker(select)
Opponent
Setting display directly on select::picker(select) shows the picker even while the select is closed (quote: "If you style select::picker(select), it will make the picker visible even when the select is closed!")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — Unsupported browsers fall back to the OS menu, which has no custom picker layout to style

Writing ::picker(select) { display: grid } the way you would for any element, the option grid is spread across the page before the menu is ever opened. Picker layout styles must wait for the open state.

Support Customizable <select>: Limited

mwg:custom-select-picker-layouts:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Always wrap <selectedcontent> in a <button> CorrectionPartialLimited Custom select picker layouts · Hidden preconditions of new features
Action
To show rich content for the selected option in the trigger, put <selectedcontent> inside the <button> within <select>
Opponent
Without a wrapping <button>, <selectedcontent> just becomes ordinary content in the picker (quote: "the <selectedcontent> will just become part of the picker, like any other content element.")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — Unsupported browsers fall back to the OS menu, whose trigger button still shows the selected text

You want the closed dropdown to show the chosen color swatch, drop in <selectedcontent>, and it ends up in the option list while the trigger still shows text only. It only works inside the trigger <button>.

Support Customizable <select>: Limited

mwg:custom-select-picker-layouts:3 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Give base-select an explicit width CorrectionPartialLimited Custom select picker layouts · Layout unexpectedly overflows or shifts
Action
Set a fixed width or flex/grid constraints after enabling appearance: base-select.
Opponent
base-select removes longest-option sizing, so selected content changes width and shifts layout. (quote: "Setting appearance: base-select removes the default browser behavior of sizing the select based on its longest option width. You may need to set a fixed width or use flex/grid constraints to prevent layout shifts.")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — The fallback OS menu sizes to the widest option automatically without layout shifts

Customizable select no longer reserves width for the longest option.

Support Customizable select: Limited.

mwg:custom-select-picker-layouts:4 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Add geometric left/right navigation while preserving linear up/down navigation CorrectionPartialLimited Custom select picker layouts · Hand-built controls lose native behavior
Action
Handle Left and Right with getBoundingClientRect(), retain sequential Up and Down, and do not apply grid role to the picker.
Opponent
Native select only handles linear Up/Down, so Left/Right do nothing; removing sequential navigation can hide options from screen-reader users. (quote: "A native <select> only handles linear Up/Down arrow navigation, so Left/Right do nothing in the open picker and Up/Down still navigate items sequentially, regardless of rows and columns.")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — The fallback OS menu is already a vertical list where Up/Down linear arrow navigation works normally

Actual geometry handles irregular grids and RTL better than parsing CSS track strings.

Support Customizable select: Limited.

mwg:custom-select-picker-layouts:5 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Let inputs, textareas and selects grow and shrink with field-sizing: content New capabilityPartialNewly Form fields that automatically fit their contents · Size doesn't follow content
Idea · brainstorm'Inputs that grow as you type' used to need JS mirroring or measuring → chat composers, inline rename fields and tag inputs can hug their text in pure CSS, looking like plain text yet editable on click
Action
Set field-sizing: content on <input>, <textarea> and <select>, resetting inherited global width/height to auto
Opponent
Form controls have fixed sizes by default regardless of how much the user enters, so overflow scrolls inside the field; auto-growing in older browsers needs a Grid trick with a hidden pseudo-element mirroring the input in real time (quote: "Their sizes remain constant, regardless of the amount of content the user enters or selects.")
Fallback
Loses the main benefit — Falls back to fixed default sizing where overflow scrolls inside the field unless using a complex CSS Grid mirror hack
Unlock
Previously auto-growing fields required copying styles and syncing text to a hidden mirror via JS; one CSS property resizes inputs, textareas, and selects automatically

A comment box is three lines tall, and writing more means scrolling inside a tiny frame; making it grow used to mean duplicating styles and syncing text into a hidden element with JS. One property replaces that whole mirror. The guide recommends most apps simply accept fixed sizes in older browsers rather than force a fallback.

Support field-sizing: Newly (2026-06-16; Chrome 123, Edge 123, Firefox 152, Safari 26.2)

mwg:form-fields-automatically-fit-contents · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Give auto-width fields both a minimum and a maximum width CorrectionPartialNewly Form fields that automatically fit their contents · Layout unexpectedly overflows or shifts
Action
Set min-inline-size (e.g. 15ch) and max-inline-size (e.g. 50ch) on text inputs using field-sizing: content, and max-inline-size on <select>
Opponent
Without a minimum, an empty field collapses to zero width and can't be clicked; without a maximum, it grows indefinitely and breaks the page layout (quote: "A minimum size prevents the input from collapsing to a width of zero when empty (making it unclickable), and a maximum size ensures it doesn't expand indefinitely and break the page layout.")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — With fixed default sizing, fields do not collapse to zero width or grow endlessly to break layouts

An empty input with no placeholder simply vanishes once field-sizing is on; paste a long URL and the field pushes the whole row off screen. Give it a sensible range to grow within.

Support field-sizing: Newly (2026-06-16)

mwg:form-fields-automatically-fit-contents:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Give auto-growing textareas a fixed width CorrectionPartialNewly Form fields that automatically fit their contents · Layout unexpectedly overflows or shifts
Action
When a <textarea> uses field-sizing: content, set an explicit width (width: 50ch or 100%) so only height follows content, plus min-block-size: 3lh and max-block-size: 10lh
Opponent
If a textarea can auto-size horizontally, one with a long placeholder abruptly shrinks when the user types the first character (quote: "a textarea with a long placeholder will abruptly shrink horizontally when the user types a single character")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — With fixed default sizing, textareas already have a fixed width and will not suddenly narrow

A full-sentence placeholder stretches the textarea that wide; the moment the user starts typing, the placeholder disappears and the box snaps to one character wide. Pin the width and let it grow downward until a scrollbar appears at the cap.

Support field-sizing: Newly (2026-06-16)

mwg:form-fields-automatically-fit-contents:3 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Cancel flex and grid stretching for content-sized fields CorrectionPartialNewly Form fields that automatically fit their contents · Size doesn't follow content
Action
Set align-self:start or justify-self:start on field-sizing controls inside grid and flex layouts.
Opponent
Grid and flex layouts implicitly stretch children, preventing fields from shrinking to their content. (quote: "Grid and Flexbox layouts often implicitly stretch their children to fill available space.")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — With fixed default sizing, fields stretch with their container normally without refusing to shrink

The container alignment default can defeat auto-sizing even after explicit widths are reset.

Support field-sizing: Newly since 2026-06-16.

mwg:form-fields-automatically-fit-contents:4 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Explicitly mark helper buttons type="button" so they don't submit the form CorrectionWinN/A Forms · Forms submit unintentionally
Action
Set type="button" on secondary or helper buttons in a form (show password, add row, clear); keep the main submit button as type="submit"
Opponent
A <button> inside <form> defaults to type="submit", so a helper button without a type submits the form when pressed (quote: "explicitly set type="button" on secondary or helper buttons so they don't default to type="submit".")
Fallback
Not needed — type is existing HTML behavior; no fallback issue

Halfway through a form, the user presses a helper like 'Show password' and the whole form submits, just because that button had no type and fell back to submit. The opposite applies to the main submit button: don't make it type="button".

Support N/A (the guide has no browser support data at all)

mwg:forms · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Send sensitive data with POST, not GET CorrectionWinN/A Forms · Sensitive data leaks
Action
Use method="POST" for sensitive data and state-changing forms; reserve GET for idempotent requests like search
Opponent
Sending sensitive data with GET exposes it in browser history and server logs (quote: "DON'T use GET for sensitive data (it exposes data in history/logs).")
Fallback
Not needed — Submission methods are existing HTML behavior without browser feature support issues

GET appends form fields to the URL, and URLs persist in browser history and in server and proxy access logs. Fine for a search query, not for ID numbers or passwords.

Support N/A (the guide has no browser support data at all)

mwg:forms:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Use a checkbox, not a radio, for a single yes/no choice CorrectionWinN/A Forms · Wrong native control for the job
Action
Pick controls by option count: a checkbox for a single binary toggle, radios for 2–5 exclusive options, <select> only for 6+, <datalist> for large or dynamic lists
Opponent
A single radio button can't be unchecked once checked (quote: "Can be checked and unchecked with space unlike a radio button, which gets stuck once checked.")
Fallback
Not needed — Choosing controls by option count uses existing HTML markup

'Subscribe to the newsletter' built as a single radio: the user clicks it, changes their mind, and has no way to undo it. The wrong control brings the wrong behavior. The guide maps each situation to a suitable native element with an option-count table.

Support N/A (the guide has no browser support data at all)

mwg:forms:3 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Do not visually reorder form controls with CSS CorrectionWinN/A Forms · Visual order drifts from DOM order
Action
Keep visual, DOM, and keyboard Tab order aligned.
Opponent
CSS reordering makes keyboard focus jump around a different visual order. (quote: "DON'T use CSS to visually reorder form controls away from their DOM/keyboard Tab order.")
Fallback
Not needed — Layout and DOM order are entirely up to the author

Tab order must match the visible form sequence.

Support No support data; N/A.

mwg:forms:4 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Do not auto-submit when an option changes CorrectionWinN/A Forms · Forms submit unintentionally
Action
Require an explicit submit action after select, radio, or checkbox changes.
Opponent
Changing an option submits or shifts context before the user can review. (quote: "DON'T auto-submit a form when a user changes <select>, radio buttons, or checkbox without an explicit submit action.")
Fallback
Not needed — Whether to auto-submit is up to your script logic

Arrow-key browsing must not unexpectedly submit the form.

Support No support data; N/A.

mwg:forms:5 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Use text and inputmode for numeric identifiers CorrectionWinN/A Forms · Wrong native control for the job
Action
Use type="text" and inputmode="numeric" for card numbers, ZIP codes, and OTPs.
Opponent
Number inputs cause scroll and spinner issues and remove leading zeros. (quote: "DON'T use type="number" for credit cards, ZIP codes, or one-time passcodes (causes UI scroll issues and removes leading zeros).")
Fallback
Not needed — inputmode is already Widely available; numeric keyboards have no fallback issue

These values are identifiers, not quantities.

Support No support data; N/A.

mwg:forms:6 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Keep a single value in one field instead of auto-advancing boxes CorrectionWinN/A Forms · Autofill fails
Action
Use one text input for OTPs, phone numbers, and cards; style the single field as segments if desired.
Opponent
Auto-advancing multi-box inputs hinder autofill, paste, and accessibility. (quote: "DON'T split a single value (such as a 6-digit OTP, phone number, or credit card) across multiple <input> boxes that auto-advance focus on keypress.")
Fallback
Not needed — Single field vs. split inputs is a form markup choice without browser feature support issues

Visual segments do not require separate data controls.

Support No support data; N/A.

mwg:forms:7 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Allow paste and autocomplete on authentication fields CorrectionWinN/A Forms · Autofill fails
Action
Keep paste enabled and assign correct autocomplete tokens to passwords, codes, and authentication fields.
Opponent
Blocking these features prevents password managers and system code suggestions from working. (quote: "DON'T block copy-and-paste (paste events) or disable autocomplete on passwords, verification codes, or other authentication fields.")
Fallback
Not needed — Whether to intercept paste is a form policy choice

Security fields especially benefit from password managers.

Support No support data; N/A.

mwg:forms:8 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Use :user-invalid instead of raw :invalid for error styling CorrectionWinN/A Forms · Announcements mistimed or unreliable
Action
Keep native constraints but trigger visual errors with :user-invalid.
Opponent
Raw :invalid marks empty required fields as errors before interaction. (quote: "DON'T use the raw :invalid CSS pseudo-class alone for error styling to ensure empty required fields are not marked as invalid before the user interacts with the form.")
Fallback
Not needed — Which error pseudo-class to style is existing CSS usage

A newly opened form should not start covered in errors.

Support No support data; N/A.

mwg:forms:9 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Do not disable submit to block validation CorrectionWinN/A Forms · Hiding or disabling locks people out
Action
Keep submit enabled to reveal errors; disable only after valid submission to prevent duplicates.
Opponent
Disabled submit prevents users from triggering validation and learning what to fix. (quote: "DON'T disable submit buttons to block validation; let users submit and highlight errors.")
Fallback
Not needed — Whether to disable the submit button is a form behavior choice

A disabled button gives no explanation.

Support No support data; N/A.

mwg:forms:10 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Do not validate and announce errors on every keystroke CorrectionWinN/A Forms · Over-announcing
Action
Validate on submit or blur and clear resolved errors on input without per-keystroke live announcements.
Opponent
Per-keystroke errors and announcements interrupt users while they are still typing. (quote: "DON'T trigger validation errors or aria-live error announcements on every keystroke while the user is typing")
Fallback
Not needed — Validation timing is decided by your script

Intermediate values during typing are often necessarily invalid.

Support No support data; N/A.

mwg:forms:11 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Use at least 1rem form text to prevent iOS zoom CorrectionWinN/A Forms · Layout unexpectedly overflows or shifts
Action
Set font:inherit and font-size:max(1rem,1em) on controls.
Opponent
Small control text triggers automatic iOS zoom on focus and disrupts layout. (quote: "staying at least 1rem(16px) to prevent iOS zoom.")
Fallback
Not needed — Font-size settings use existing CSS without browser feature support issues

The keyboard and submit controls stay in view.

Support No support data; N/A.

mwg:forms:12 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Hide native controls visually without display:none CorrectionWinN/A Forms · Visually hidden but still reachable
Action
Use the clipped 1px visually-hidden recipe for custom checkbox and radio inputs.
Opponent
display:none removes the real control from the accessibility tree. (quote: "NOT display: none, which removes them from the accessibility tree.")
Fallback
Not needed — Visually hiding native elements uses an established CSS pattern

Custom visuals still operate a real native input.

Support No support data; N/A.

mwg:forms:13 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Keep a server fallback for AJAX forms CorrectionWinN/A Forms · Hand-built controls lose native behavior
Action
Make native form submission work first, then enhance with preventDefault() and fetch.
Opponent
A JavaScript-only submission path makes the form unusable when scripts fail. (quote: "DON'T block page submission if JS fails; ensure server-side fallback.")
Fallback
Not needed — Native form submission paths are an existing capability

Progressive enhancement starts with a working native path.

Support No support data; N/A.

mwg:forms:14 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Remove inactive wizard steps from Tab and the accessibility tree CorrectionWinN/A Forms · Visually hidden but still reachable
Action
Hide inactive steps with hidden, display:none, or inert and move focus to the new step.
Opponent
Inactive controls remain reachable even though users cannot see or should not use them. (quote: "DON'T leave inactive wizard steps in the keyboard Tab order or accessibility tree")
Fallback
Not needed — Hiding steps can use existing hidden, display: none, or inert

Focus must follow the visible wizard state.

Support No support data; N/A.

mwg:forms:15 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Keep wizard inputs and buttons clear of the mobile keyboard CorrectionWinN/A Forms · Popovers cover instructions
Action
Place focused controls and primary buttons in the upper viewport or use scroll-padding.
Opponent
The virtual keyboard can obscure active inputs and navigation buttons. (quote: "design layouts so that the mobile keyboard does not obscure inputs or buttons")
Fallback
Not needed — Layout configuration is up to the author

Users need not dismiss the keyboard to find the next step.

Support No support data; N/A.

mwg:forms:16 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Check isComposing (plus keyCode 229) before Enter-to-submit so you don't send mid-IME composition CorrectionPartialLimited IME-safe Enter to submit · Forms submit unintentionally
Action
In a custom Enter keydown handler, return early without calling form.requestSubmit() when event.isComposing or event.keyCode === 229; applies to <textarea> and single-line <input> with custom Enter handling
Opponent
When typing Chinese, Japanese or Korean with an IME, Enter confirms the conversion candidate; a script that submits on Enter sends the message mid-conversion (quote: "the user's message is sent while they are still converting characters, resulting in incomplete, fragmented, or incorrect messages.")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — On Safari where isComposing resets early, keyCode === 229 or a timestamp window still blocks premature submit during IME composition

In a chat box you type a word, press Enter to confirm the conversion, and half-converted kana or phonetic input gets sent. Native implicit submission from an <input> is already handled by the browser; it's custom keydown handlers that break. The guide also warns that migrating old keyCode === 13 checks to key === 'Enter' without these two checks introduces the bug.

Support api.KeyboardEvent.isComposing: Limited (Chrome 56, Edge 79, Firefox 31; not Safari)

mwg:ime-safe-enter-submit · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Call preventDefault() in custom Enter-to-submit to avoid submitting twice CorrectionWinN/A IME-safe Enter to submit · Forms submit unintentionally
Action
Call event.preventDefault() first in the Enter keydown handler, then call requestSubmit() yourself
Opponent
Enter's default action inserts a newline in a <textarea> and triggers implicit submission for an <input> in a <form>, so with your own submit it goes out twice (quote: "in an <input> inside a <form> it triggers the browser's implicit submission, which would submit a second time.")
Fallback
Not needed — preventDefault() is existing DOM behavior without browser feature support issues

Search bars, inline rename fields and command palettes often handle Enter themselves; forget to block the default and the browser submits the form again. preventDefault() also stops a textarea from adding a stray newline before sending.

Support N/A (no support data for preventDefault() in the guide; its only support data is for isComposing)

mwg:ime-safe-enter-submit:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Flag required-field errors with :user-invalid, not in red on page load CorrectionWinWidely Required field feedback · Announcements mistimed or unreliable
Action
Add required to fields and trigger error styles and error text with :user-invalid, starting messages with an icon whose text alternative is 'Error' so color isn't the only cue
Opponent
Marking required fields as errors as soon as the page loads is confusing; a field should only look invalid after the user tried and failed (quote: "Marking required fields with an error state immediately upon page load can be confusing.")
Fallback
Not needed — :user-invalid is already Widely available; no fallback needed
Unlock
Previously :invalid flagged empty fields on load; :user-invalid marks errors only after a failed user attempt

The form opens with a red border on every required field, telling users they've done something wrong before they've started. :user-invalid follows the browser's interaction timing so errors only show when they should. ARIA state still needs a small sync script.

Support :user-valid/:user-invalid: Widely (2023-11-02)

mwg:required-field-feedback · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Sync aria-invalid from :user-invalid, not checkValidity() CorrectionWinWidely Required field feedback · Announcements mistimed or unreliable
Action
Start fields at aria-invalid="false" and set "true" on blur or failed submit based on el.matches(':user-invalid')
Opponent
checkValidity() is already false when a user merely tabs through an untouched field, so assistive tech is told about errors too early (quote: "deriving it from :user-invalid, not checkValidity(), which is already false when a user tabs through an untouched field.")
Fallback
Not needed — :user-invalid is already Widely available; ARIA syncing uses existing script patterns

The red border appears only after interaction, but if the ARIA sync script uses checkValidity(), a screen reader user hears 'invalid' on every field they tab through. Both sides need the same criterion. Firefox and Safari also expose empty required fields as invalid from load, so the starting value must be an explicit "false".

Support :user-valid/:user-invalid: Widely (2023-11-02)

mwg:required-field-feedback:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Attach the error message to aria-describedby only while the field is invalid CorrectionWinWidely Required field feedback · Announcements mistimed or unreliable
Action
Point the field's data-error at the error message id and have the script list it in aria-describedby only while the field is invalid
Opponent
Referencing the error message in the markup makes the hidden message get read from page load (quote: "A reference in the markup would read the hidden message from page load.")
Fallback
Not needed — :user-invalid is already Widely available; when to mount error messages is up to your script

The error element sits in the page, hidden with CSS, with the description already wired up, so the first focus reads 'This field is required.' Attaching it only when invalid means users hear the current state.

Support :user-valid/:user-invalid: Widely (2023-11-02)

mwg:required-field-feedback:3 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Announce errors through one delayed polite live region CorrectionWinWidely Required field feedback · Announcements mistimed or unreliable
Action
Send field errors to one page-level polite live region after a short delay, and focus the first invalid field after failed submission.
Opponent
A live region that is merely shown rather than changed is not announced reliably, and simultaneous messages can talk over the next field. (quote: "a live region that is shown, rather than changed, isn't announced reliably.")
Fallback
Not needed — Live regions are an existing ARIA mechanism without browser feature support issues

The live region must exist from page load and receive a text update, not merely become visible.

Support :user-valid and :user-invalid: Widely.

mwg:required-field-feedback:4 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Hide required-field asterisks from assistive technology CorrectionWinWidely Required field feedback · Over-announcing
Action
Wrap visual asterisks in aria-hidden spans, explain the convention once, and retain the required attribute.
Opponent
required already announces the state, so an exposed asterisk adds redundant speech. (quote: "wrap it in <span aria-hidden="true">*</span>, because the required attribute already makes screen readers announce "required".")
Fallback
Not needed — required and aria-hidden are existing HTML behaviors

Visual decoration should not duplicate a programmatic state.

Support :user-valid and :user-invalid: Widely.

mwg:required-field-feedback:5 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Keep submit enabled so the browser reveals required errors CorrectionWinWidely Required field feedback · Hiding or disabling locks people out
Action
Leave submit enabled before validity; activation triggers :user-invalid and focuses the first invalid field.
Opponent
A disabled submit prevents users from requesting validation and receiving error and focus guidance. (quote: "Unlike disabled buttons, keep your submit button enabled. If the user clicks it, the browser will automatically trigger :user-invalid on all empty required fields and focus the first one.")
Fallback
Not needed — :user-invalid is already Widely available; enabling or disabling the submit button is up to the form

A disabled button says only that submission is unavailable, not what needs fixing.

Support :user-valid and :user-invalid: Widely.

mwg:required-field-feedback:6 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Use base-select for rich options instead of a custom menu New capabilityStalemateLimited Rich media picker (customizable select) · Hand-built controls lose native behavior
Idea · brainstormAssignee menus with avatars, color swatches, and plan descriptions can use native select and form submission. Firefox falls back to plain text.
Action
Set appearance: base-select on select and its picker; put SVG, images, titles, and descriptions in options, and mirror the selected content in the button.
Opponent
Native option markup was stripped to plain text, forcing heavy custom components for rich options. (quote: "Prior to this API, the browser would strip tags from <option> tags and render only plain text.")
Fallback
Loses the main benefit — Fall back to plain-text native options, which still can't do icon and description layouts
Unlock
Previously native <option> could hold only plain text, forcing heavy custom widgets for icons/descriptions; now options hold rich HTML with native behavior

Rich options no longer require abandoning native select.

mwg:rich-media-picker · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

mwg:rich-media-picker:4 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Give base-select an explicit width CorrectionPartialLimited Rich media picker (customizable select) · Layout unexpectedly overflows or shifts
Action
Set a fixed width or flex/grid constraints after enabling appearance: base-select.
Opponent
base-select removes longest-option sizing, so the select changes width with the selected content and shifts layout. (quote: "Setting appearance: base-select removes the default browser behavior of sizing the select based on its longest option width.")

mwg:rich-media-picker:5 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Use select:user-invalid to delay required-select errors CorrectionWinWidely Validate select menus after interaction · Announcements mistimed or unreliable
Action
Give the first option an empty disabled value and trigger errors with :user-invalid and success with :user-valid.
Opponent
Standard validation marks an empty default option invalid on page load, creating visual noise. (quote: "standard validation flags the field as invalid immediately if the default option has an empty value. This can create visual noise.")

mwg:select-menu-interaction · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Calculate slider fill in CSS with progress() and attr() New capabilityPartialLimited Brand-consistent range sliders · JS patches in styling state
Idea · brainstormVolume, rating thresholds, and budget sliders can keep ratio calculations in CSS and change bounds through HTML attributes. Safari needs a JS fallback.

Read min and max with typed attr(), calculate the percentage with progress(), and feed it to the track gradient; use ::-moz-range-progress in Firefox.

Only the current value still needs JavaScript synchronization.

Use separate rule blocks for ::-webkit-slider-thumb and ::-moz-range-thumb, and likewise for tracks.

Idea · brainstormA data table's 'show all rows' or a settings page's tabs can be built up front and kept hidden at no cost, appearing instantly on click. For a concrete statement of the blocker see mwg:faster-spa-view-transitions.
