Set ::view-transition { pointer-events: none; } and, when only specific elements transition, :root { view-transition-name: none; } to disable the default root transition
Opponent
During a transition the screen is an overlay of snapshots and elements can't be interacted with; the root transition animates between two identical full-page snapshots, so the whole page is unclickable (quote: "during the transition, elements are not interactive")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — Browsers without view transitions update the DOM directly; supporting ones disable root transitions and snapshot pointer events to keep the page interactive

Only one list item is moving, yet every button on the page ignores clicks for that half second.

Support View transitions: Newly

mwg:group-element-transitions:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Highlight text with the CSS Custom Highlight API without touching the DOM New capabilityPartialNewly Highlight text ranges · Rebuilding the DOM loses state
Idea · brainstormMarking text used to mean splitting the DOM → a notes app's in-page search, live syntax coloring in code blocks, and other people's selections in collaborative editing can sit on top of framework-rendered content without conflict
Action
Collect text nodes with a TreeWalker, create Ranges, wrap them in new Highlight(...ranges), register with CSS.highlights.set("search-results", h), and style with ::highlight(search-results); use priority for overlaps
Opponent
The fallback of wrapping matches in <mark> modifies the DOM, so you must take care to keep event listeners and not break the document structure (quote: "This modifies the DOM, so take care to preserve event listeners and avoid breaking the document structure.")
Fallback
Loses the main benefit — Fall back to wrapping text in <mark>, which still requires DOM changes and protecting listeners and structure
Unlock
Style arbitrary text ranges for search hits or syntax highlighting without altering the DOM or splitting text nodes

In-page search, syntax coloring, and collaborative cursors used to split text into wrapper elements, and each split risked losing someone else's listeners and structure. Now ranges are just a registration and the browser paints the style.

Support Custom highlights: Newly (2026-03-24), Supported by: Chrome 105, Edge 105, Firefox 149, Safari 17.2

mwg:highlight-text-ranges · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Use <mark> for meaningful highlights, not custom highlights CorrectionPartialNewly Highlight text ranges · Visual change without semantics or focus
Action
Reserve custom highlights for transient visuals like search results or syntax coloring; use <mark> when the highlight itself carries meaning; pair error highlights with a wavy underline, label, or icon
Opponent
Custom highlights are purely presentational and not in the accessibility tree, so screen reader users miss whatever the highlight conveys (quote: "Custom highlights are purely presentational and are not exposed to the accessibility tree.")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — Semantic highlights should already use Widely supported <mark> and visual cues so accessibility trees stay intact

The same yellow background is just a hint in search results but may be the key point in a tutorial; leave the latter to a highlight and screen reader users miss it.

Support Custom highlights: Newly

mwg:highlight-text-ranges:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Clear old highlights before registering new ones CorrectionPartialNewly Highlight text ranges · Hidden preconditions of new features
Action
Call CSS.highlights.clear() before each set(); cache the text-node list and rebuild it only when the DOM content changes
Opponent
Without clearing, stale ranges stay on the page (quote: "to avoid stale ranges persisting on the page")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — Unsupported browsers never register highlights, leaving neither plain text nor <mark> fallbacks with stale ranges

The search term changed but the previous term is still lit up; the registry doesn't expire on its own.

Support Custom highlights: Newly

mwg:highlight-text-ranges:3 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

::highlight() only accepts a few properties CorrectionPartialNewly Highlight text ranges · Hidden preconditions of new features
Action
In ::highlight() use only color, background-color, text-decoration, text-shadow, -webkit-text-stroke-*, and -webkit-text-fill-color
Opponent
Properties such as background-image, font-size, or padding are ignored (quote: "Properties like background-image, font-size, or padding are ignored.")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — Use only supported color and text-decoration properties in highlights, while <mark> fallbacks allow full box-model styling

A highlight isn't an element and has no box; designs that bold, outline, or resize the text can't be done here.

Support Custom highlights: Newly

mwg:highlight-text-ranges:4 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Register gradient stops with @property so a pointer-following spotlight opens and closes smoothly New capabilityPartialNewly Interactive content reveal · Size changes jump instead of animating
Idea · brainstormSizes inside gradients couldn't transition → a portfolio "flashlight over the sketch", a circular magnifier on before/after images, or an X-ray effect on product shots can open and close smoothly with just a little coordinate JS
Action
Register --inner-size and --outer-size as <length-percentage> with @property, reference them in mask-image: radial-gradient(circle at var(--mouse-x) var(--mouse-y), …), transition only the sizes, and update only the position variables on pointermove
Opponent
Browsers without @property can't interpolate values inside radial-gradient, so the spotlight snaps between on and off (quote: "the movement will jump between on and off states because they cannot interpolate values inside a radial-gradient")
Fallback
Loses the main benefit — Fall back to a mask with unregistered variables; the spotlight still works but opening and closing jumps
Unlock
Registering gradient stops as typed properties lets minimal pointer JS drive smooth spotlight reveal transitions

Numbers inside a gradient can't animate by default, so the spotlight could only pop in. Registering the stops as typed properties tells the browser how to transition between sizes.

Support Registered custom properties: Newly (2024-07-09); Masks: Widely

mwg:interactive-content-reveal · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

The spotlight is decoration only; it must not hide or gate content CorrectionWinN/A Interactive content reveal · Hiding or disabling locks people out
Action
Set pointer-events: none on the mask layer; keep the underlying content fully visible and keyboard-reachable by default, with the spotlight as an extra for pointer users
Opponent
Using the effect to obscure or gate essential content leaves keyboard-only and assistive technology users without it, and the mask layer blocks clicks on controls beneath (quote: "Never use this effect to obscure or gate essential content from keyboard-only or assistive technology users.")
Fallback
Not needed — Underlying content stays visible by default with pointer-events: none on the overlay, keeping all devices able to reach it

"Move over it to see" is fun, but only for mouse users; the content itself must be open to everyone first.

Support Accessibility requirement: no support data in the guide, recorded as N/A

mwg:interactive-content-reveal:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Preview an action's effect before it's pressed with interestfor New capabilityPartialLimited Interest-triggered action previews · Only reachable by hover
Idea · brainstormPreviews needed hand-written hover/focus/delay handling → theme pickers, font menus, and filter buttons can "try it on while hovering, revert on leave", including on keyboard focus. Native in Chromium only, others via polyfill
Action
Put interestfor="target-id" on a button or link, listen for interest / loseinterest on the target and apply or undo the preview based on event.source; style with :interest-source / :interest-target, tune delays with interest-delay-start / -end
Opponent
The guide only says previewing actions before committing can help, without saying when older approaches go wrong (quote: "It can be beneficial to provide users a preview of their actions before they commit to them.")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — When unsupported, load the interestfor polyfill with :is() and CSS variables so Firefox/Safari still preview actions
Unlock
Buttons and links declare interest relationships directly in HTML to preview actions before committing without hover/delay scripts

Seeing the effect by hovering "Bold" or "Italic" used to mean wiring hover, focus, leave, and delays by hand. Now "interest" is a declared relationship, and the browser manages events and delays.

Support Interest invokers: Limited availability, Supported by: Chrome 149, Edge 149; Unsupported in: Firefox, Safari

mwg:interest-triggered-action-previews · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Don't announce interest-triggered previews in a live region CorrectionPartialLimited Interest-triggered action previews · Over-announcing
Action
Let the preview be the affordance; don't announce apply/unapply through a live region
Opponent
Interest fires just from moving the pointer or tabbing past nearby buttons, so apply/unapply announcements become noise that drowns out content users care about (quote: "apply/unapply announcements quickly become noise that can drown out content the user actually cares about")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — Skipping live-region announcements avoids screen-reader noise while previews still run across native and polyfilled browsers

Sweep the mouse across a row of buttons and the screen reader says "previewing" five times; people who can't see the preview gain nothing from hearing it.

Support Interest invokers: Limited

mwg:interest-triggered-action-previews:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Build tooltips that don't close menus with popover="hint" and interestfor New capabilityStalemateLimited Show a tooltip when hovering · Popups interfere with each other
Idea · brainstormTooltips used to need hand-wired hover/focus/Esc and fought with menus → icon-button help, term definitions, and link preview cards can be almost fully declarative and readable while a menu is open. Native in Chromium only, others via polyfill
Action
Use <div popover="hint" id> for the tooltip and interestfor on the triggering <button> / <a>; the trigger becomes an implicit anchor, positioned with position-area: block-start and position-try-fallbacks: flip-block; toggletips also get popovertarget with popovertargetaction="show"
Opponent
With an auto popover as a tooltip, hovering across it closes an open menu (quote: "hovering across a toggletip must not close an open menu, which an auto popover would")
Fallback
Loses the main benefit — Fall back to popover=auto, where opening a tooltip may still close an already open menu
Unlock
HTML attributes and CSS anchor positioning build non-menu-closing tooltips triggered on hover, focus, or long-press with auto-flipping

Tooltips and menus are both popovers, so opening one used to close the other. hint is a third type for glance-and-go content, opened by hover, focus, or long-press without disturbing what's already open.

Support Interest invokers: Limited (Chrome 149, Edge 149); popover="hint": Limited (Chrome 151, Edge 151, Firefox 153; Unsupported in: Safari); Anchor positioning core properties: Newly. The guide says "Supported by: Safari 27 (Sep 2026). Unsupported in: Chrome, Edge, and Firefox.", which is the misleading group status, see lines/ui-components/app-menus.md; this line doesn't use position-visibility

mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Don't add aria-expanded to triggers that do something else CorrectionPartialLimited Show a tooltip when hovering · Semantic structure misrepresents the page
Action
When the trigger navigates or performs an action (a link, a button with its own action), give the hint role="tooltip" and the trigger aria-describedby, not aria-expanded; only toggletips that open the hint on press use aria-expanded, synced from the popover's toggle event
Opponent
A trigger announced as "collapsed" suggests Enter will expand it, but Enter navigates or acts (quote: "A trigger announced as "collapsed" suggests Enter would expand it, but Enter navigates or acts.")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — Running a single upfront ARIA wiring script before polyfill load exposes accurate roles and relationships across all browsers

Browsers and screen readers don't yet expose interestfor semantics consistently, so you add ARIA yourself; add one wrong aria-expanded and a link is announced as something expandable.

Support Interest invokers: Limited

mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Add nothing when the hint matches the accessible name CorrectionPartialLimited Show a tooltip when hovering · Over-announcing
Action
Normalize whitespace and compare the hint text with the trigger's accessible name; if equal, add no description; only when the trigger has no name, point aria-labelledby at the hint
Opponent
For example an icon button with aria-label="Bold" and a "Bold" tooltip: a description identical to the name is read twice (quote: "A description identical to the name would be read twice.")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — The upfront script compares names across all native and polyfilled browsers and skips identical descriptions to avoid double-reading

The most common tooltip text is the button's own name; wire it up as a description too and the screen reader says "Bold, Bold".

Support Interest invokers: Limited

mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips:3 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Hints exposed as descriptions may only hold content that's fine to miss CorrectionPartialLimited Show a tooltip when hovering · Announcements mistimed or unreliable
Action
Put only skippable content such as link previews or action descriptions in description hints; information users need goes in a toggletip or inline
Opponent
Not every screen reader reads descriptions while browsing; NVDA skips them in browse mode by design (quote: "Not every screen reader reads descriptions when moving through the page (NVDA skips them in browse mode by design)")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — Essential info goes into toggletips or inline text with polyfill support so every browser and screen reader can reach it

Put "why this field is required" in a hover hint and sighted users occasionally see it, while NVDA users never hear it.

Support Interest invokers: Limited

mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips:4 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

toggle doesn't bubble: sync aria-expanded with a capturing listener CorrectionPartialLimited Show a tooltip when hovering · Non-bubbling events never arrive
Action
Handle popover toggle events with a single capturing listener on document and update every trigger pointing at that hint; treat the popover as the source of truth instead of syncing from interest / loseinterest
Opponent
toggle doesn't bubble, so a normal listener on document never fires; the popover can also be closed by Esc, light dismiss, or another invoker (quote: "A bubbling listener on document never fires; use the capture phase (or a listener per popover).")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — Using a capturing toggle listener on document keeps aria-expanded synced across both native and polyfilled popovers

Syncing from interest events seems enough, until Esc closes the hint and the trigger still announces "expanded".

Support Popover: Newly; Interest invokers: Limited

mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips:5 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Without hint support, switch toggletips to auto in beforetoggle CorrectionPartialLimited Show a tooltip when hovering · No guard for unsupported browsers
Action
Detect support by setting popover = "hint" on a probe element and reading it back; if unsupported, in a capturing beforetoggle listener switch the opening toggletip to popover = "auto"
Opponent
Browsers without hint treat it as manual: a tooltip opened by keyboard focus can stay open when another is opened by hover, and a click-opened toggletip has no interest to lose and never closes (quote: "so a manual fallback would never close")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — Switching unsupported hint toggletips to auto in capturing beforetoggle lets Safari dismiss clicked toggletips normally

An invalid attribute value silently becomes manual: it opens but won't close. The type has to change in beforetoggle; changing it while open closes it.

Support popover="hint": Limited (Unsupported in: Safari)

mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips:6 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Without the anchor positioning polyfill, gate inset: auto inside @supports CorrectionPartialNewly Show a tooltip when hovering · Popups detach from their trigger
Action
Without the polyfill, put inset: auto, margin: 0, and position-area inside @supports (position-area: block-end), or give a @supports not fixed bottom bar; with the polyfill, set explicit anchor-name / position-anchor on each trigger and hint pair because the polyfill doesn't support implicit anchors
Opponent
Setting inset: auto unconditionally overrides the popover's default centering while position-area is ignored, leaving the tooltip in the top-left corner or over its trigger (quote: "leaving the popover stranded at (0, 0) or overlapping its trigger")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — Gating resets with @supports keeps fallback centering or bottom bars intact, or explicit anchors work with the polyfill

The inset reset meant to pin the tooltip to its button leaves only the "reset" half in browsers that don't understand anchors.

Support Anchor positioning core properties: Newly (misleading group status, see lines/ui-components/app-menus.md; this line doesn't use position-visibility)

mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips:7 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Use closedby="any" to dismiss a modal dialog from its backdrop New capabilityPartialLimited Light-dismiss a dialog · Hand-built controls lose native behavior
Idea · brainstormImage lightboxes, quick previews, and settings panels can gain native-feeling dismissal with one attribute instead of coordinate calculations. Safari still needs the fallback.
Action
Open <dialog closedby="any"> with showModal(). Where unsupported, fall back to a script that checks coordinates only when the event target is the dialog itself.
Opponent
With hand-written light dismissal, clicking the dialog background or padding also targets the dialog, so a target-only check closes it by mistake. (quote: "This distinguishes between a click on the backdrop vs a click on the dialog's background/padding.")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — When closedBy is missing, a click-coordinate fallback checks the dialog bounding box so Safari also light-dismisses cleanly
Unlock
Add one HTML attribute to enable modal backdrop light-dismiss and Esc closing without hand-calculating click bounding boxes

Backdrop and dialog padding look alike to a click handler. Native light dismissal removes that ambiguity.

Support <dialog closedby>: Limited; Chrome/Edge 134 and Firefox 141, unsupported in Safari.

mwg:light-dismiss-a-dialog · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Let nested components handle Escape before the dialog CorrectionWinN/A Light-dismiss a dialog · Popups interfere with each other
Action
Menus and comboboxes inside a modal dialog should handle Escape while focused.
Opponent
A component tries to close its list with Escape but inadvertently closes the whole dialog. (quote: "this may lead to the dialog being inadvertently closed")
Fallback
Not needed — Modal dialog Esc behavior is universal, and focused inner widgets intercepting Esc prevent accidental dialog dismissal

Pressing Escape to cancel a selection should not make a half-completed form disappear.

Support Modal dialog Escape behavior: no support data in the guide; N/A.

mwg:light-dismiss-a-dialog:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

closedby only works for dialogs opened with showModal() CorrectionPartialLimited Light-dismiss a dialog · Hidden preconditions of new features

Opponent
A non-modal dialog has no backdrop and does not trigger light dismissal. (quote: "as they do not have a backdrop and won't trigger light-dismiss")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — Backdrop light-dismiss applies only to modals, and Safari without closedby is covered by the coordinate fallback

The attribute can be present but appear broken because the dialog has no outside backdrop layer.

Support <dialog closedby>: Limited.

mwg:light-dismiss-a-dialog:3 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Opponent
Clipping and masking also clip the element's own focus outline. (quote: "Both also clip the element's own focus outline")

Not needed — Clipping and focus outlines use foundational CSS; drawing focus rings on an unclipped parent works across browsers

Support clip-path and mask-image: no support data in the guide; N/A.

mwg:motion · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Not needed — Overview points direction only with no support data; decorative effects can remain static where unsupported
Unlock
Pure CSS creates non-essential scroll-linked decorative effects instead of JavaScript scroll listeners

This overview points to the detailed scroll progress and parallax guides.

mwg:motion:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Use View Transitions between complex layout states New capabilityWinN/A Motion · Size changes jump instead of animating

The guide only says transitions can be seamless, without an observable failure in the old approach. (quote: "Use **View Transitions** to animate between complex layout states seamlessly.")

Not needed — Overview points direction only with no support data; specific transition fallbacks depend on individual guides
Unlock
Seamlessly animate between complex layout states without manually orchestrating transition state

This overview points to the grouped-element and directional-navigation transition guides.

mwg:motion:3 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Declare transition-behavior separately after transition CorrectionWinN/A Motion · Shorthands or linked properties reset settings

List opacity, display, and overlay in transition, then declare transition-behavior: allow-discrete on a later line.
Opponent
Putting it in or before the shorthand resets it or breaks it in older browsers. (quote: "Separate after transition so the shorthand doesn't reset it or fail in older browsers")

Not needed — No support data in this guide; writing it separately after transition keeps older browsers from discarding the whole rule

The same shorthand-reset trap appears in the element entry and exit guide.

Support No support data in this guide; N/A.

mwg:motion:4 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Do not add aria-pressed when the pause button label already changes CorrectionWinN/A Motion · Semantic structure misrepresents the page

Provide a keyboard-operable pause button for motion lasting over five seconds; when its label switches between Pause and Play, omit aria-pressed.
Opponent
Combining a changing label with aria-pressed makes screen readers announce a pressed Play button. (quote: "or screen readers announce a pressed "Play" button")

Not needed — Button labels and ARIA follow existing standards; updating label text alone ensures screen readers announce state accurately

A pressed Play button leaves listeners unable to tell whether playback is active.

Support ARIA usage: no support data in the guide; N/A.

mwg:motion:5 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Leave content in its final state when animation is disabled CorrectionWinN/A Motion · Hiding or disabling locks people out
Action
Default to static content and add animation only under no-preference, ensuring elements end in their final state.
Opponent
Disabled animation can leave content at its initial hidden state, such as opacity: 0, including focus and selection indicators. (quote: "so content isn't left hidden (for example, at opacity: 0)")
Fallback
Not needed — prefers-reduced-motion is standard practice; defaulting to static states and opting into motion stays safe everywhere

If a fade-in starts transparent, disabling the animation must not leave it transparent forever.

Support prefers-reduced-motion: no support data in the guide; N/A.

mwg:motion:6 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Use event.animation in animation and transition events; feature-detect with animation in AnimationEvent.prototype.

Filtering event.target.getAnimations() by name misses unnamed WAAPI animations, conflates same-name animations, and cannot distinguish pseudo-elements. (quote: "event.target always points to the originating DOM element, so it does not distinguish between animations running on the element itself versus one of its pseudo-elements")
Fallback
Not needed — This guide gives feature detection only; fallback filters event.target.getAnimations() by name or property

Support event.animation: feature detection is given but no support data; N/A.

mwg:motion:7 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

When cleanup depends on animation completion, continue immediately if getAnimations() returns an empty list or retain a short opacity transition.
Opponent
With animation disabled, none, or zero duration, animationend and transitionend never fire, so dependent removal or hiding never happens. (quote: "animationend and transitionend never fire")
Fallback
Not needed — getAnimations() and short opacity transitions use existing capabilities so cleanup finishes without waiting on animation events

A notification cannot close if its close logic waits for an event that reduced motion prevents.

Support No support data in the guide; N/A.

mwg:motion:8 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Move elements with moveBefore() without reloading iframes or losing focus New capabilityStalemateLimited Move a DOM element without losing state · Rebuilding the DOM loses state

mwg:move-dom-element-without-losing-state · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

mwg:parallax-scroll-effects:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Convert a JS easing function or SVG path into linear() stops, store them in a custom property, and supply a duration.

Simple ease-in and cubic-bezier() curves cannot express bounces or springs. (quote: "making it impossible to create complex physics-based effects like bounces or springs")

mwg:physics-based-easing:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Idea · brainstormMobile filters, image viewers, and confirmations can close like native app surfaces without leaving the page. Safari is still unsupported.

Opponent
Early dialogs responded to Escape but not mobile back controls, and there was no good way to implement those close requests manually. (quote: "it could be dismissed with the <kbd>Esc</kbd> key, but not other platform controls such as a back button/gesture on mobile … There is no good way to implement close requests from mobile back button/gestures")
Fallback
Loses the main benefit — Safari lacks mobile back-button/gesture dismissal with no reliable workaround, leaving Esc and close buttons to dismiss
Unlock
Modal <dialog> elements opened with showModal() automatically respond to mobile back buttons/gestures and AT dismiss gestures

mwg:platform-controls-dismiss-dialog · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Idea · brainstormLocking background scroll used to mean touching the root element and paying with layout jumps → lightboxes, confirmations, and full-screen settings panels can lock the background in pure CSS, and the page stays put with sticky intact on close. Safari only when the dialog content overflows

Set overscroll-behavior: contain on dialog:modal; set overflow: hidden on dialog::backdrop to make it a non-scrollable scroll container, then overscroll-behavior: contain on it too
Opponent
showModal() blocks clicks and focus but not scrolling: scrolling over the backdrop or past the end of the dialog scrolls the page; the old fix of overflow: hidden or position: fixed on <html>/<body> removes the scrollbar, shifts layout and jumps the scroll position (quote: "Mutating root overflow removes the page scrollbar (causing horizontal layout shift), can reset or jump the page scroll position, and can break position: sticky elements")
Fallback
Loses the main benefit — Safari only stops chaining when dialog content scrolls, so dragging backdrop/non-overflowing modals still scrolls the page cleanly without layout hacks
Unlock
Two CSS declarations trap scroll chaining inside modal <dialog> and ::backdrop without mutating root overflow or breaking sticky UI

With a modal open, one swipe on the dimmed backdrop quietly scrolled the article behind it; the body-lock trick made the whole page jump sideways and broke sticky headers. Two CSS declarations now keep scrolling inside the dialog; Safari is the remaining gap.

Support overscroll-behavior (on non-scrollable scroll containers): Limited availability. Supported by: Chrome 144, Edge 144, Firefox 150. Unsupported in: Safari

mwg:prevent-page-scroll-under-modal-dialog · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Don't feature-detect overscroll support on non-scrollable containers with @supports CorrectionPartialLimited Prevent the page underneath a modal dialog from scrolling · Feature detection is unreliable

Every modern browser recognises the syntax and returns true, even if it only enforces the property when content overflows (quote: "All modern browsers support the overscroll-behavior: contain property syntax and return true, even if they only enforce it when content overflows.")

Keeps core behavior — Treating scroll containment as progressive enhancement without @supports branching preserves focus trapping and scrollable containment everywhere

mwg:prevent-page-scroll-under-modal-dialog:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

This lack of continuity makes it harder for users to track relationships between elements.")
Fallback
Loses the main benefit — Without support the DOM updates instantly, the thumbnail-to-image animation is lost and the image jumps again
Unlock

mwg:same-document-transitions · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Each view-transition-name may belong to only one element before and after; clear temporary names afterwards CorrectionPartialNewly Same-document transitions · Transitions skipped or broken

Ensure each name maps to one element before and after the transition; remove names added via .selected after transition.finished
Opponent
With two or more elements sharing a name, the DOM updates immediately with no transition (quote: "If there are 2 or more elements with a given view-transition-name, the DOM will be updated to the new state immediately, without a transition.")

The first click animated; back on the list, clicking another card did nothing — the name left on the previous item collided with the new one.

Support View transitions: Newly

mwg:same-document-transitions:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Transitions don't manage focus: move it to the new heading yourself CorrectionPartialNewly Same-document transitions · Hiding or disabling locks people out
Action
After the DOM update or when transition.finished resolves, focus the new view's heading or container (tabindex="-1"), including in the no-transition branch
Opponent
If focus stays on an element hidden or removed during the transition, it is abandoned and keyboard and AT users lose context (quote: "If focus remains on an element that is hidden or removed during the transition, focus is abandoned, leaving keyboard and assistive technology users without context.")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — Unsupported branches also shift focus after DOM updates, preserving keyboard and screen-reader context everywhere

Pressing a thumbnail by keyboard morphed beautifully into the detail page, but focus fell back to the top and the next Tab started over.

Support View transitions: Newly

mwg:same-document-transitions:3 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Use fit-content on transitioning text so snapshots don't stretch CorrectionPartialNewly Same-document transitions · Transitions skipped or broken
Action
Set width: fit-content on the transitioning text in both views; for elements that change aspect ratio set height: 100% on ::view-transition-old/new() and use object-fit if needed
Opponent
By default the old and new snapshots cross-fade inside a group that stretches to fit both, distorting them (quote: "By default, the browser cross-fades the old and new snapshots within a group that stretches to fit both.")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — fit-content sizing and aspect settings act as normal layout when unsupported and switch views cleanly without distortion

The title flying from list to detail got squashed and then stretched. A snapshot is an image; it takes whatever width its group has.

Support View transitions: Newly

mwg:same-document-transitions:4 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Use element.startViewTransition() to keep a transition inside a component instead of covering the page New capabilityPartialLimited Scoped component transitions · Transitions skipped or broken
Idea · brainstormA small component's animation used to freeze the whole page → dashboard cards can each animate sorting, adding and removing at the same time while the header and floating toolbars stay clickable. Chromium only for now
Action
Call element.startViewTransition() on the component root, name children with view-transition-name: match-element, and add view-transition-scope: all to repeated component containers so names don't leak
Opponent
document.startViewTransition() attaches the overlay to :root, so during the transition the page can't be clicked, transitions can't run concurrently, and fixed headers and open popovers are covered (quote: "blocks pointer events on the rest of the page, prevents concurrent transitions, and obscures position: fixed headers or open [popover] elements")

Unlock

While a sidebar list was animating a reorder, the header buttons couldn't be clicked and an open menu was hidden under the transition. Scoping it to the component leaves the rest of the page alone — but only Chromium can do it for now.

Keeps core behavior — Moving existing nodes preserves morph matching in supporting browsers while updating lists properly in non-transition fallbacks

mwg:scoped-component-transitions:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Keeps core behavior — Browsers without scoped transitions run DOM updates directly without promise errors; supporting ones stay safe when caught

A user clicked "Sort" repeatedly and the console filled with unhandled rejections.

Support Element-scoped view transitions: Limited

mwg:scoped-component-transitions:3 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Opting out of self-participation disables automatic overflow clipping, so transitioning children spill outside the component (quote: "opting out of self-participation disables automatic overflow clipping.")

Support Element-scoped view transitions: Limited

mwg:scoped-component-transitions:4 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

An outer transition started from a parent or the document captures and animates the scope element and everything inside it (quote: "the outer transition will capture and animate the scope element and everything inside it.")

Keeps core behavior — When scoped transitions are unsupported, immediate DOM updates avoid outer/inner transition capture conflicts altogether

Support Element-scoped view transitions: Limited

mwg:scoped-component-transitions:5 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Idea · brainstorm"Scroll there, then act" used to mean guessing or wiring scrollend → guided tours, line-by-line code walkthroughs and map lists can await each scroll and highlight in straight-line code. Chromium only for now
Action
Make the handler async and await element.scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth' }) (or scrollTo(), scrollBy()), then add the highlight, start the animation or move focus
Opponent
Guessing scroll duration with setTimeout() fires too early on long scrolls and too late on short ones; a hand-wrapped scrollend promise never resolves when the target is already in view (quote: "fires too early on long scrolls and too late on short ones"; "scrollend does not fire when the target is already in view and no scrolling occurs")

Keeps core behavior — When return values are not Promises, wait on scrollend with an idle timer so Firefox/Safari also await scroll end
Unlock

Opponent
When a new scroll interrupts a smooth scroll, the browser resolves rather than rejects all pending promises, so the old follow-up still runs (quote: "the browser aborts the ongoing smooth scroll and **resolves** (does not reject) all pending scroll promises on that container.")

Keeps core behavior — Incrementing operation ID guards work identically with the Firefox/Safari Promise fallback so rapid clicks never misfire

A user clicked three sections quickly and all three flashed their highlight.

Support Scroll method promises: Limited

Opponent
focus() scrolls again by default, fighting the scroll that just finished (quote: "so the browser does not jump or scroll a second time.")
Fallback
Not needed — preventScroll is an existing standard option applying equally after awaiting either native or fallback scroll Promises

The smooth scroll centred the section, then focusing the heading jerked it to the top of the screen.

When the document's root scroller is scrolling, Chrome resolves the scrollIntoView() promise too early (quote: "Chrome has a bug where the Promise returned by scrollIntoView() resolves too early when it is the document's root scroller that is scrolling.")

Idea · brainstormEntry and exit effects used to need IntersectionObserver ratios per element → horizontal galleries, timelines and product rows can scale and fade each item as it enters and leaves, rewinding automatically when scrolled back

Write separate @keyframes for entry (fill backwards) and exit (fill forwards), bind them with animation-timeline: view() to the element's own visibility, and limit them with animation-range: entry, exit; or use range selectors like entry 0% and exit 100% in one @keyframes

The guide doesn't say what breaks in the old approach; it only says the fallback is IntersectionObserver and native is more performant (quote: "In browsers with built-in support for scroll-driven animations, ALWAYS use the native CSS implementation as those are more performant.")

Keeps core behavior — When unsupported, IntersectionObserver updates styles by intersection ratio, or decorative effects stay static

mwg:scroll-target-on-load:4 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Use named view-timelines and timeline-scope so one set of sections drives another set's animations New capabilityPartialNewly Scrollytelling · Scroll-linked effects rely on JS listeners
Idea · brainstorm"Read this paragraph and the graphic changes" used to need a library like scrollama → year-in-review pages, product tours and data journalism can let each paragraph drive a pinned layer, rewinding when scrolled back
Action
Put named timelines like view-timeline: --tl-1 block on the tracked sections, publish them with timeline-scope on a common ancestor (often html), bind the animated elements with animation-timeline: --tl-1, and set exact ranges with animation-range
Opponent
The guide doesn't say what breaks in the old approach; it only says this needs no JavaScript and follows scroll position rather than a clock (quote: "The animations are controlled by the scroll position, not a time-based clock, which ensures they are always in sync with the user's scroll.")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — When unsupported, IntersectionObserver drives transforms by visibility ratio, or decorative stories remain visible statically
Unlock
Pure CSS named view-timeline and timeline-scope link sections across the DOM to drive scroll-synced storytelling without JS

Text on the left, a picture on the right that changes with each section. The text is the timeline and the picture the animation; they needn't be parent and child — timeline-scope ties them together.

Support Scroll-driven animations: Baseline Newly available (since 2026-10-27)

mwg:scrollytelling · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Add animation-range: 0% 100% to the check to filter partial support CorrectionPartialNewly Scrollytelling · Feature detection is unreliable
Action
Write @supports ((animation-timeline: scroll()) and (animation-range: 0% 100%))
Opponent
Checking only animation-timeline lets partially supporting browsers through (quote: "The (animation-range: 0% 100%) check **MUST** be included here, to filter out browsers with only partial support.")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — Adding the animation-range check excludes partial browsers cleanly into the IntersectionObserver fallback

Detection said yes, but the ranges were ignored and the image appeared at the wrong section.

Support Scroll-driven animations: Newly

mwg:scrollytelling:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Put animation-timeline after the animation shorthand CorrectionPartialNewly Scrollytelling · Shorthands or linked properties reset settings
Action
Write the animation shorthand first, then animation-timeline and animation-range
Opponent
The shorthand resets the timeline (quote: "declare animation-timeline and animation-range *after* it to prevent the shorthand from resetting the timeline.")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — Declaring after the shorthand preserves named timelines while @supports routes unsupported browsers to JS fallback

Every section's animation played through by itself on load.

Support Scroll-driven animations: Newly

mwg:scrollytelling:3 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Content must stay visible if the fallback script doesn't run or reduced motion is requested CorrectionPartialNewly Scrollytelling · Hiding or disabling locks people out
Action
Attach the fallback's "hidden first" styles only to a .scroll-fallback class added by script; under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce force opacity: 1 and transform: none
Opponent
Hiding sections by default while waiting for animation leaves content invisible forever if the script doesn't run (quote: "The CSS only hides the sections once this class is set, so they stay visible if the script doesn't run")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — Hiding only when the fallback class is added and respecting reduced motion keeps story content visible if scripts fail

The script was blocked and the whole right column stayed blank; half the story was missing.

Support Scroll-driven animations: Newly

mwg:scrollytelling:4 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Hide content with <details> or hidden="until-found" so find-in-page still reaches it New capabilityPartialLimited Search hidden content · Hiding or disabling locks people out
Idea · brainstormCustom tab contents used to be invisible to search → settings pages with many tabs, tabbed code samples on docs sites and product spec switchers can be hit directly by Ctrl+F and text-fragment links that switch to the right tab. Safari falls back to expanding everything
Action
Prefer <details> for ordinary disclosure; when the controls live elsewhere in the DOM, styling must be fully custom, or content won't be re-hidden, use hidden="until-found" and sync related state in beforematch (e.g. set aria-expanded="true", close other panels)
Opponent
Content hidden with display: none or visibility: hidden is completely unreachable to screen readers and Find in page (quote: "they also make that content completely inaccessible to screen readers and browser features like "Find in page".")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — Standard folds use Widely supported <details>; when until-found is unsupported on Safari, JS expands all content to keep it searchable
Unlock
Hidden accordion or panel content stays searchable via Find-in-page and text-fragment links, auto-expanding and syncing state

Text inside tabs and custom accordions couldn't be found with Ctrl+F, and shared text-fragment links didn't open. With until-found the browser reveals the match itself and fires beforematch so buttons can catch up.

Support <details>: Widely. hidden="until-found": Limited availability. Supported by: Chrome 102, Edge 102, Firefox 148. Unsupported in: Safari

mwg:search-hidden-content · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Don't add display or visibility to hidden="until-found" elements CorrectionPartialLimited Search hidden content · Hiding or disabling locks people out
Action
Leave hiding entirely to hidden="until-found"; don't add display: none, visibility: hidden or similar
Opponent
Those styles break the native behaviour and remove the content from the search index for good (quote: "This breaks the native functionality and permanently hides the content from the search index.")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — Safari already uses the expanded fallback unaffected by hiding styles, while supporting browsers stay searchable without overrides

An extra display: none "to be safe" made until-found do nothing.

Support hidden="until-found": Limited

mwg:search-hidden-content:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Put borders, padding and backgrounds on an inner wrapper, not the until-found element CorrectionPartialLimited Search hidden content · Layout unexpectedly overflows or shifts
Action
Apply borders, padding and backgrounds to a child wrapper
Opponent
Applied directly to the hidden="until-found" element they leave layout shifts or visual remnants while hidden (quote: "This prevents unintended layout shifts or visual remnants while the element is hidden.")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — Placing borders and padding on an inner wrapper keeps layout clean under both native hiding and Safari expansion fallback

A collapsed panel still showed an empty border and a strip of height.

Support hidden="until-found": Limited

mwg:search-hidden-content:3 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Don't hide sensitive or irrelevant data with hidden="until-found" CorrectionPartialLimited Search hidden content · Sensitive data leaks
Action
Keep sensitive information, internal data tokens and content that shouldn't be searchable out of until-found sections
Opponent
until-found content is found and revealed by find-in-page (quote: "**DO NOT** use hidden="until-found" for sensitive information, internal data tokens, or irrelevant data that should not be exposed via search.")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — Sensitive data never belongs in client markup, keeping both native search and Safari expanded fallback equally leak-free

Thinking hidden meant safe, internal fields were turned up by a user's search.

Support hidden="until-found": Limited

mwg:search-hidden-content:4 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Move <tr> elements when sorting; don't rebuild the tbody CorrectionWinWidely Sortable table · Rebuilding the DOM loses state
Action
When a <button> in a column header is clicked, move the existing <tr> elements within <tbody> and mark the sorted column with aria-sort
Opponent
Rebuilding <tbody> with innerHTML or a re-render on sort loses focus and row state and breaks view transitions (quote: "DO NOT re-render the <tbody> or <table> on sort; it discards focus and state and breaks view transitions.")
Fallback
Not needed — Reordering existing rows and aria-sort use Widely available capabilities, sorting cleanly without newer move/transition/command APIs

This is the table version of dynamic-sort. The guide also puts the button inside <th> rather than making <th> clickable, keeps aria-sort on one column only, and keeps the button label as the column name instead of "Sort ascending". Invoker commands are recommended over a click listener per button, but without saying what concretely goes wrong with the old way.

Support Invoker commands: Newly (2025-12-12)

mwg:sortable-table · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Compare by column type, not formatted strings CorrectionWinWidely Sortable table · Comparing the wrong type
Action
Declare each column's type with data-type and compare numbers and dates by their underlying values
Opponent
Comparing the formatted strings on screen sorts numbers and dates in the wrong order (quote: "DO NOT sort formatted strings when the underlying values are numbers or dates.")
Fallback
Not needed — Comparing raw values by data-type with numeric diff or Intl.Collator uses standard JS supported everywhere

"1,200" sorting before "950", or "2026/1/10" before "2025/12/3", is what string comparison does. The guide has each column declare its type instead of guessing from content.

Support —

mwg:sortable-table:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Don't preventDefault() when there is no candidate in that direction; let the browser scroll CorrectionWinN/A Spatial navigation (directional keypad focus) · Familiar platform controls have no effect
Action
Intercept arrow keys only in composite widgets; only when a candidate is found call preventDefault(), move the roving tabindex and scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest', inline: 'nearest' }); otherwise return; ignore modifier keys, already-handled events and targets that use arrows themselves (editable fields, sliders)
Opponent
Overriding arrow keys unconditionally kills native scrolling and breaks accessibility (quote: "Overriding arrow keys unconditionally breaks accessibility (WCAG 1.4.10).")
Fallback
Not needed — Arrow keys and scrollIntoView are standard event handling; calling preventDefault() only when a candidate exists works everywhere

A media rail got arrow-key navigation; with focus on the last row, pressing Down no longer scrolled the page.

Support No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:spatial-navigation · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Pick the next focus from live geometry on each keypress, not index or DOM order CorrectionWinN/A Spatial navigation (directional keypad focus) · Visual order drifts from DOM order
Action
On keypress read getBoundingClientRect() for the current and candidate elements (no caching), test direction by edges, prefer candidates overlapping on the perpendicular axis, else score gap + w * perpendicular offset; only consider elements passing checkVisibility()
Opponent
In asymmetric, wrapped or grid layouts index mapping picks wrong; hidden elements can have a zero-size rect at (0, 0) and become accidental up/left targets (quote: "In asymmetrical, wrapped, or grid layouts, index-based mapping fails."; "Hidden elements can have a zero-sized rect at (0, 0) and must not become accidental up or left targets.")
Fallback
Not needed — getBoundingClientRect() and checkVisibility() are standard DOM queries; recomputing geometry per keypress works everywhere

Wide and narrow cards mixed: Right jumped to the start of the next line, and a hidden button made Up fly to the top-left corner.

Support No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:spatial-navigation:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Roving tabindex needs composite-widget roles; screen readers ignore tabindex alone CorrectionWinN/A Spatial navigation (directional keypad focus) · Semantic structure misrepresents the page
Action
Give the container and items roles that fit the use: grid/gridcell, tablist, listbox/option, tree, treegrid or combobox
Opponent
Without matching roles, roving tabindex doesn't work with screen readers (quote: "Roving tabindex only works with screen readers when the container and items have appropriate composite-widget roles and states (e.g. grid/gridcell, listbox/option); tabindex alone isn't enough.")
Fallback
Not needed — Composite ARIA widget roles and roving tabindex follow established standards recognized across assistive tech

Keyboard users loved it; screen reader users heard a pile of unrelated buttons and never learned arrows worked.

Support No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:spatial-navigation:3 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Use composedPath()[0] to find where the key came from, not just e.target CorrectionWinN/A Spatial navigation (directional keypad focus) · Encapsulation boundaries break relationships
Action
Take the innermost target with e.composedPath()[0] and check it against :read-write, select, input[type="range"], [role="slider"] to see if it uses arrows itself
Opponent
e.target can be retargeted to a shadow host, hiding that the key came from an input inside (quote: "Use e.composedPath()[0] rather than only e.target, because e.target can be retargeted to a shadow host.")
Fallback
Not needed — composedPath() and standard control selectors work across browsers to identify inner text inputs accurately

Pressing Left inside a custom element's text field to move the caret jumped focus to the neighbouring card.

Support No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:spatial-navigation:4 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Build swipe-to-remove with scroll snap and IntersectionObserver, not hand-written pointer events CorrectionWinWidely Swipe to remove · Hand-built controls lose native behavior
Action
Make each row a three-column (left spacer, content, right spacer) horizontal track with scroll-snap-type: x mandatory; an IntersectionObserver rooted at the track watches the content, popping the icon below activateThreshold and committing with the collapse animation below commitThreshold
Opponent
Driving a transform yourself with pointerdown/pointermove/pointerup loses the momentum, snap-back and keyboard scrolling native scrolling gives for free (quote: "You'll lose the momentum, snap-back, and keyboard scrolling that native scrolling gives you for free.")
Fallback
Not needed — Scroll snap and observers are already Widely available, replacing manual pointer dragging across all browsers

A hand-built swipe-to-delete didn't coast after release and judged speed oddly. Making the row a snapping horizontal scroller gives native feel; the code only watches how much content is still on screen.

Support Scroll snap, Intersection observer, MutationObserver, Web animations: Baseline Widely available

mwg:swipe-to-remove · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Set overscroll-behavior-x: none on the track to stop over-swipes triggering Back CorrectionPartialLimited Swipe to remove · Native scroll gestures don't fit the use
Action
Set overscroll-behavior-x: none on each row's horizontal track
Opponent
Without it, an over-swipe can trigger the iOS/Android back-navigation gesture (quote: "Without it, an over-swipe can trigger the browser's back-navigation gesture on iOS/Android.")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — The three-column track is genuinely horizontally scrollable, so Safari also honors overscroll-behavior-x: none against back gestures

mwg:swipe-to-remove:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

proximity lets the row rest half-scrolled with the action background half visible (quote: "With proximity, the row can rest partially scrolled, leaving the action background half-visible.")

mwg:swipe-to-remove:5 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Opponent
Safari's scroll-latching bug: removing the node while momentum is still resolving lets the next row inherit the scroll and immediately scroll off-screen (quote: "causes the next item (which slides up into this one's place) to inherit the scroll and immediately scroll itself off-screen.")
Fallback
Not needed — inert and GestureEvent detection defer removal specifically for Safari momentum while other browsers remove immediately

Set up each row when it enters the viewport, and wire later rows with MutationObserver CorrectionWinWidely Swipe to remove · Wrong lifecycle assumptions

An outer IntersectionObserver calls setupItem() the first time a row enters view and pauses the inner observer when it leaves; a MutationObserver on the <ul> registers newly added rows

Fallback
Not needed — IntersectionObserver and MutationObserver are already Widely available for lazy wiring and dynamic rows

mwg:swipe-to-reveal · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Use overscroll-behavior: chain on the outer swipe wrapper: scroll still chains, but no bounce New capabilityStalemateLimited Swipe to reveal · Native scroll gestures don't fit the use
Idea · brainstormNested scrollers used to force a choice between bouncing and trapping → vertical feeds can contain swipe-to-act rows, side-swipeable cards or horizontal chip rows that don't bounce at the edge and hand extra scroll to the page. Safari still bounces

Unlock
Suppress local rubber-band bounce on the outer swipe wrapper while still chaining excess scroll to ancestor scrollers

mwg:swipe-to-reveal:6 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

mwg:accordion · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Avoid exclusive <details name> so content doesn't jump out of view CorrectionPartialNewly Accordion · Layout unexpectedly overflows or shifts

Opponent
In an exclusive accordion, opening one item closes another and content shifts out of view, which seriously affects screen-magnifier users (quote: "They also can cause content to shift out of the user’s view which can cause significant problems for those using screen magnifiers.")

<details name> only became Baseline in 2024, yet the guide advises against it. What makes this line unusual is that the opponent is not an old technique but a side effect of a new feature. When exclusivity is truly needed, the guide says to use it only as a last resort.

mwg:accordion:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Collapse with ::details-content to keep find-in-page and animation New capabilityPartialNewly Accordion · Hiding or disabling locks people out
Idea · brainstormA long page can be fully collapsed while Ctrl+F still finds and expands matches, with an opening animation. Long docs, FAQs and weekly notes no longer have to choose between collapsing and being findable.
Action
Collapsed content lives in ::details-content and is hidden with content-visibility: hidden rather than display: none
Opponent
Hiding collapsed content with display: none makes it unfindable by find-in-page and its height cannot animate (quote: "While closed it is hidden with content-visibility: hidden, not display: none, which is what keeps it findable and lets its size animate.")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — When interpolate-size is unsupported, panels open/close instantly without height animation
Unlock
Collapsed content hidden with content-visibility: hidden stays searchable in-page and animates height cleanly

Once a collapsed section is display: none, Ctrl+F cannot find it. A closed <details> hides its content with content-visibility: hidden instead, so the content is still there and searchable, and the browser opens it automatically on a search hit. The ::details-content pseudo-element is what lets you select, style and animate the height of the collapsed part. Conversely, use display: none deliberately when the content should not be searchable.

Support <details> auto-opens on find-in-page match: Chrome 97, Firefox 148, Safari 26.2 (Safari does not scroll to the matched text correctly, WebKit bug 304174; not mapped to any web-features feature, so no Baseline label); ::details-content: Newly (2025-09-16); transition-behavior: Newly (2024-08-06)

mwg:accordion:3 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Pin menus to their trigger with anchor positioning New capabilityPartialNewly Application menu bar · Popups detach from their trigger
Idea · brainstormA desktop-style File/Edit/View menu bar can be built almost declaratively with popover plus anchor positioning, with menus attached to their buttons. Web tools can look and behave like desktop programs.
Action
Each menu in a menu bar (File/Edit/View) is a popover placed next to its trigger with CSS anchor positioning
Opponent
Without anchor positioning a popover falls back to the centered viewport position, detaching the menu from its trigger, and a centered submenu covers its parent (quote: "Never ship that for a menu: it detaches the menu from its trigger, and a centered submenu covers its parent.")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — When anchor positioning is unsupported, script positioning keeps menus tethered next to their triggers
Unlock
Popovers tether directly next to trigger buttons or submenus with CSS anchor positioning

A menu bar is one widget: one Tab stop, left/right arrows switch menus, focus previews. Each menu must sit under its trigger, but a native popover defaults to the middle of the viewport. The guide's support section says anchor positioning is "supported only in Safari 27", but that is the status of the whole feature group, not of the properties this guide uses; see the details.

Support Anchor positioning core properties: Newly (2026-01-13; position-anchor 2026-09-14). The guide says "Supported by: Safari 27. Unsupported in: Chrome, Edge, and Firefox.", which is the lowest common support of the whole web-features anchor-positioning group (325 sub-features); Chrome and Firefox only lack the position-visibility: anchor-valid / anchor-visible values (Chrome 157 beta, not Firefox), which this guide does not use. Popover: Newly (2025-01-27); focusgroup: Limited (Chrome/Edge 150)

mwg:app-menus · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Keep separators so breadcrumbs read as a hierarchy, not siblings CorrectionWinWidely Breadcrumbs · Appearance implies the wrong structure
Action
Build breadcrumbs with <nav> + <ol>, with separators generated in CSS and hidden from assistive tech
Opponent
Pill or segmented styles without separators look like tabs or filters (items on the same level), not a hierarchy (quote: "Pills, tags and a segmented bar without one look like tabs or filters (items on the same level), not a hierarchy.")
Fallback
Not needed — HTML lists and CSS separators are already Widely available; no fallback needed

Designers often want breadcrumbs to look more like a button row, and the result implies the wrong structure. The guide treats separators as essential and uses ol rather than ul to express order.

Support —

mwg:breadcrumbs · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Use border-shape so borders and focus rings follow slanted segments New capabilityStalemateLimited Breadcrumbs · Focus or state indicators disappear
Idea · brainstormSlanted, arrow or notched shapes can carry their borders and focus rings along the shape, without sacrificing accessibility to clip-path. Chromium only for now.
Action
Draw slanted or arrow-shaped segments with corner-shape / border-shape, with borders and focus outlines following the shape
Opponent
Cutting shapes with clip-path also clips borders and focus outlines; forced-colors mode removes the background, so a clipped segment loses its outline (quote: "clip-path clips borders and outlines, so under the fallback use a color/background change plus negative outline-offset for focus instead of an outside outline.")
Fallback
Loses the main benefit — Falls back to clip-path, losing shape-following borders and focus outlines
Unlock
border-shape renders borders and focus outlines directly along irregular shapes

Arrow-shaped breadcrumbs used to rely on clip-path, so the keyboard focus ring was cut off and whole segments vanished in high-contrast mode. The new properties make the border itself the shape, but Firefox and Safari do not support them yet.

Support corner-shape: Limited (Chrome/Edge 139); border-shape: Limited (Chrome/Edge 147)

mwg:breadcrumbs:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

When a card has a lot of text or other actions, use a stretched link instead of wrapping it in <a> CorrectionWinN/A Build a card · Over-announcing
Action
Wrap the <article> in one <a> only when the whole card is one destination and the text is short; otherwise make only the heading's .card-link a link and stretch its hit area with ::after and inset: 0
Opponent
When the whole card is inside the link, the link's accessible name is all of the card's text (quote: "Because the link's accessible name is all of the card's text, keep the content short")
Fallback
Not needed — Support status is N/A; no fallback needed

Screen reader users had to hear the whole summary, author and date in the link list to learn which article it was. Making only the heading a link and stretching the hit area fixes both hearing and clicking.

Support No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:card · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

"Read more" links need a full name that starts with the visible text CorrectionWinN/A Build a card · Semantic structure misrepresents the page

Write Read more<span>(visually hidden) about poached eggs</span>; add no other links repeating the heading's URL
Opponent
Identical "read more" links can't be told apart in a screen reader's link list (quote: "identical "read more" links are ambiguous in a screen reader's link list.")
Fallback
Not needed — Support status is N/A; no fallback needed

The link list showed ten "Read more" entries.

mwg:card:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Don't change layout-affecting properties when a choice card is selected CorrectionWinN/A Build a card · Layout unexpectedly overflows or shifts
Action
Put a checkbox or radio in <label class="card"> and use :has(> :checked) to change only a transparent border's colour, outline or box-shadow
Opponent
Changing border-width, padding or font-weight on selection makes the card and its neighbours jump (quote: "Never change layout-affecting properties such as border-width, padding, or font-weight on selection, because the card and its neighbors jump")

Not needed — Support status is N/A; no fallback needed

Selecting a plan card nudged the whole row two pixels to the right.

mwg:card:3 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Only one stretched link per card; lift other interactive elements individually CorrectionWinN/A Build a card · Stacking contexts change layering
Action
Add .card-link to exactly one link per card; give other a, button, input etc. position: relative; z-index: 1 by element type, never z-index on whole containers
Opponent
With several stretched links the last one covers the card; z-index on a whole container captures clicks that do nothing (quote: "each would stretch its own overlay and the last one would capture the whole card"; "Do NOT apply z-index to entire containers as that would make them capture pointer events that don't produce any action.")
Fallback
Not needed — Support status is N/A; no fallback needed

Clicking "Save" on a card opened the article; clicking the footer's empty space did nothing.

mwg:card:4 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Lay out cards with the card itself as the query container, not the viewport or grid parent CorrectionWinN/A Build a card · Layout depends on the wrong measurement
Action
Set container-type: inline-size on the card and adapt children with @container rules; open a media side column only on cards with media via :has(> img)
Opponent
A card's real width depends on column count, gaps and so on, so parent-based breakpoints are unreliable (quote: "the card's actual width can depend on column count, gaps and so on, making parent-based breakpoints are noisy.")
Fallback
Not needed — Support status is N/A; no fallback needed

The same card was cramped in a three-column grid but used the wide layout in a sidebar.

mwg:card:5 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Loop a carousel without cloning slides by parking one with order New capabilityPartialNewly Carousel · Duplicate content confuses assistive tech
Idea · brainstormAn infinitely looping carousel without cloned slides: park one slide with CSS order and compensate the offset once scrolling settles. Content exists once, so frameworks and screen readers don't fight.
Action
For looping, use --current and CSS order to park the first or last slide beside the current one, changing only visual order without cloning or moving slides; on a marker click, set --current to initial first so the scroll runs in sequence order
Opponent
Cloning slides or moving them in the DOM for infinite looping conflicts with frameworks and makes assistive tech read duplicate content (quote: "Do not clone slides or move them in the DOM, which conflicts with frameworks and duplicates content for assistive technology.")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — When sibling-count() is unsupported, a script sets --children-count with the slide count and the carousel still loops
Unlock
Use CSS order to wrap first/last slides seamlessly for looping carousels without cloning or moving DOM

The usual infinite carousel clones a slide at each end, so screen readers hear the same slide twice. The guide instead visually parks a single slide at the other end; DOM order stays the reading and focus order, and no slide is made inert or aria-hidden. The guide also says not to use ::scroll-button() / ::scroll-marker "for now", without giving a reason.

Support Scroll snap: Widely (2020-01-15); scrollend: Newly (2025-12-12); sibling-count() and sibling-index(): Newly (2026-08-18); Scroll-driven animations: Newly (2026-10-27); overscroll-behavior: Limited (Chrome 144, Edge 144, Firefox 150; not Safari; a progressive enhancement per the guide, not split into a line)

mwg:carousel · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Restyle checkboxes with accent-color or appearance: none while keeping the native <input> New capabilityPartialLimited Styling checkboxes · Hand-built controls lose native behavior
Idea · brainstormBranded checkboxes used to mean a custom component → to-do lists, permission settings and bulk "select all (partial)" states can use native inputs that match the design, with a proper indeterminate icon
Action
Use accent-color for a simple brand colour (keeping native rendering, keyboard, validation and system focus rings); for control over shape, size and states set appearance: none on <input type="checkbox"> and draw the check and :indeterminate dash with ::before and mask
Opponent
The guide doesn't say what breaks in the old approach; it only says both techniques keep native behaviour or keep the <input> as the interactive target (quote: "This removes the native visual styling while leaving the <input> as the interactive target.")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — When accent-color is unsupported, native control colors apply, losing only brand tinting
Unlock
Style native checkboxes with brand colors directly or customize shape, size, and check icons

Branded checkboxes were often a div plus an icon. Now one accent-color line recolours them, and bolder designs can be drawn on the input itself with keyboard, forms and screen readers untouched.

Support accent-color: Limited availability. Supported by: Chrome 93, Edge 93, Firefox 92, Safari 26.2 (labelled Limited though all four engines are listed, as in mwg:brand-consistent-forms); Masks: Widely

mwg:checkbox · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Safari's accent-color doesn't guarantee check-mark contrast; test it CorrectionPartialLimited Styling checkboxes · Focus or state indicators disappear
Action
Test important accent colours in Safari in both light and dark schemes, keeping checked and indeterminate states at 3:1 contrast or more
Opponent
Safari may keep a white (light) or black (dark) check and adjust the accent behind it, which doesn't always give enough contrast (quote: "This adjustment does not always provide sufficient contrast for every supplied color")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — When accent-color is unsupported, default colors apply while checkboxes remain operable

Brand yellow with a black check was clear in Chrome; in Safari the check turned white and you could barely tell it was ticked.

Support accent-color: Limited

mwg:checkbox:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

After appearance: none, give the checkbox a size yourself CorrectionWinN/A Styling checkboxes · Hand-built controls lose native behavior

Set --checkbox-size and --checkbox-icon-size in relative units, with the icon smaller than the box
Opponent
appearance: none also removes the browser's default dimensions (quote: "appearance: none removes the browser’s default dimensions.")

Not needed — Support status is N/A; no fallback needed

Once the native look was removed, the checkbox shrank to an invisible dot.
