mwg:checkbox:3 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Don't disable the button while showing feedback CorrectionWinWidely Copy button · Hiding or disabling locks people out
Action
After copying, show feedback; on repeat clicks, reset the timer and restart the animation instead of setting the button to disabled
Opponent
Disabling the button during feedback drops keyboard focus and announces a misleading unavailable state (quote: "DO NOT disable the button while showing feedback: copying is idempotent, and disabling drops keyboard focus, announces a misleading unavailable state")
Fallback
Not needed — Clipboard API is already Widely available; no fallback needed

Disabling the button to prevent double clicks is an intuitive safeguard, but copying twice has no side effect. Disabling makes a keyboard user's next Tab start again from the top of the page.

Support Clipboard.writeText: Widely (2020-03-24)

mwg:copy-button · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Declare the copy target with Invoker Commands New capabilityPartialNewly Copy button · Wiring JS to every button
Idea · brainstormWhat a button does to another element can be written directly in HTML (command/commandfor) with no JS wiring; custom --commands let one button trigger any behaviour.
Action
Use command + commandfor to declare which element a button copies, instead of wiring JavaScript to each button
Opponent
(missing) The guide only says it replaces "per-button JavaScript wiring" without pointing to a moment where the old way fails (quote: "Declare the target with Invoker Commands (command + commandfor) instead of per-button JavaScript wiring")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — When Invoker Commands are unsupported, a click listener invokes the same copy handler
Unlock
Declare copy targets with command and commandfor without wiring JavaScript to every button

The same recommendation appears in sortable-table and accordion: declarative attributes instead of click listeners. None of the three guides says where hand-wired listeners break; they only describe the new style. Both slot 3 and the outcome are missing on this line.

Support Invoker commands: Newly (2025-12-12)

mwg:copy-button:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Hide repeated copy buttons with opacity CorrectionWinWidely Copy button · Hiding or disabling locks people out
Action
Hide the many repeated copy buttons on a page until hover or focus, using only opacity
Opponent
Hiding buttons with display: none or visibility: hidden removes them from the tab order, so keyboard users can never reach them (quote: "display: none and visibility: hidden remove the button from the tab order, so keyboard users could never reach it.")
Fallback
Not needed — CSS opacity and hover media queries are already Widely available; no fallback needed

A copy button on every code block is noisy, so they are often shown only on hover. The catch is how they are hidden: most hiding methods also take the button out of the Tab order. The guide also forbids "hiding" with aria-hidden or inert.

Support —

mwg:copy-button:3 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Changing <meta name="color-scheme"> alone does nothing; map it back to CSS with :has() CorrectionWinN/A Dark mode toggles · Cascade overrides don't match intent
Action
Keep color-scheme: light dark on :root, then override it via :root:has(> head > meta[name="color-scheme"][content="dark"]) (and light); the toggle only changes the meta's content
Opponent
The <meta> is only a presentational hint and author CSS color-scheme overrides it, so updating the meta alone is a no-op (quote: "updating the <meta> alone is a **no-op** — CSS wins.")
Fallback
Not needed — Support status is N/A; no fallback needed

The toggle changed the meta, and the page's colours didn't move. Wiring the meta back to the color-scheme property brings every colour along at once.

Support No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:dark-mode-toggle · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Apply the stored scheme with a synchronous inline script right after the <meta> CorrectionWinN/A Dark mode toggles · Content takes shape only after JS runs
Action
Place a tiny inline <script> (not a module, no defer) right after <meta name="color-scheme"> that reads localStorage and writes it back to the meta
Opponent
Applying the stored preference later flashes the wrong scheme first (quote: "To avoid a flash of the wrong scheme, apply the stored value in an inline script (NOT type=module, NOT defer) placed immediately after the <meta> element")
Fallback
Not needed — Support status is N/A; no fallback needed

A user who chose dark got flashed with white on every page load.

Support No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:dark-mode-toggle:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Compare with the system preference only when storing; never delete the stored value later just because they match CorrectionWinN/A Dark mode toggles · User settings get ignored
Action
A two-state toggle targets the opposite of what is shown; store it only if it differs from the system preference, remove the stored value if it matches; keep stored values that later match the system and don't clear them with matchMedia()
Opponent
Many systems switch by time of day, so deleting the stored value whenever they coincide makes pinning impossible; storing a value equal to the system silently pins it against future changes (quote: "removing the stored value whenever the two happen to coincide would make it impossible to pin a scheme at all."; "that would invisibly pin the scheme against future system changes.")
Fallback
Not needed — Support status is N/A; no fallback needed

Pinned to dark during the day, the preference was wiped when the OS turned dark at dusk, and the next morning the site was light again.

Support No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:dark-mode-toggle:3 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Don't branch non-colour values only on a JS-applied .dark class CorrectionWinN/A Dark mode toggles · Theme colors don't match their context
Action
Branch font weights, image sources and other non-colour values with the prefers-color-scheme media query combined with a :root:has(> head > meta[...][content="dark"]) selector
Opponent
If JS doesn't load and the OS default is dark, branches that rely only on .dark are wrong (quote: "they will be incorrect if JS doesn't load and the OS default is dark.")
Fallback
Not needed — Support status is N/A; no fallback needed

Dark OS, script blocked: a dark background with the black logo meant for light backgrounds.

Support No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:dark-mode-toggle:4 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Use native <dialog> with showModal(); don't hand-write focus traps, inert or Esc CorrectionWinN/A Dialog · Hand-written focus management
Action
Open blocking confirmations, forms and sign-in as <dialog> via command="show-modal" or showModal(); add no role="dialog", aria-modal, focus trap, inert toggling or Esc handler
Opponent
The guide only says custom overlays must rebuild these behaviours by hand, not when the rebuilt version fails (quote: "It provides the accessibility semantics, focus handling, top-layer rendering and Esc handling that custom overlays have to rebuild by hand.")
Fallback
Not needed — Support status is N/A; no fallback needed

Every project had its own modal component, each missing something different. Native dialog hands the whole bundle to the browser.

Support <dialog> itself: no support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:dialog · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Stop background scrolling under a modal with overscroll-behavior, not by locking <body> New capabilityStalemateLimited Dialog · Native scroll gestures don't fit the use
Idea · brainstormSame as mwg:prevent-page-scroll-under-modal-dialog: every modal (lightbox, confirmation, form) can lock background scroll in pure CSS without layout jumps
Action
Set overscroll-behavior: contain on dialog:modal; set overflow: hidden plus overscroll-behavior: contain on dialog::backdrop (details in mwg:prevent-page-scroll-under-modal-dialog)
Opponent
Without both rules, scrolling over the backdrop or in the dialog scrolls the page behind; locking the root with overflow: hidden or position: fixed removes the scrollbar and shifts layout (quote: "without them, scrolling over the backdrop or inside the dialog scrolls the page behind it")
Fallback
Loses the main benefit — When unsupported, the background still scrolls, losing scroll containment
Unlock
Modal dialogs prevent background page scrolling with pure CSS without locking root elements

With a delete confirmation open, one swipe scrolled the list behind it away.

Support overscroll-behavior: Limited availability. Supported by: Chrome 144, Edge 144, Firefox 150. Unsupported in: Safari

mwg:dialog:2 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Use <dialog popover> for panels people work alongside, not showModal() CorrectionPartialNewly Dialog · Wrong native control for the job

mwg:dialog:8 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Use interestfor so a link shows its preview card on both hover and focus New capabilityPartialLimited Build an interactive hovercard · Only reachable by hover
Idea · brainstormPreview cards used to need hand-written hover, focus, delay and close timers → wiki-style term previews, user profile cards and citation previews can be declarative and keyboard-reachable. Native only in Chromium, polyfill elsewhere
Action
Add interestfor="card id" to the trigger link and popover="hint" to the card; tune open/close delays with interest-delay, and set the start delay to 0 via :root:has(:interest-source) when a card is already open

The guide doesn't say what breaks in the old approach; it only says this ensures the card appears on hover and focus (quote: "This ensures the card appears on both hover and focus.")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — When unsupported, load the interestfor polyfill to preserve hover and focus previews
Unlock
interestfor opens the same hovercard preview on either pointer hover or keyboard focus

The guide never describes the old approach, so the opponent is marked missing. You still have to allocate the texture with texImage2D(), reallocate only on size change, and handle captureElementImage() throwing before the first paint.

mwg:equal-width-text-lines:4 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Let the browser paint HTML into the canvas and export it, instead of a library redrawing the DOM New capabilityStalemateLimited Exporting HTML content from canvas · Re-implementing browser rendering by hand
Idea · brainstormDashboards, styled documents and interactive charts can be saved as a PNG identical to the screen, or an HTML interaction can be recorded as video with captureStream(), without loading a screenshot library. Chrome 157+ only for now.
Action
Put the HTML to export inside <canvas content="drawable">, draw it with drawElementImage(), then export an image or video with toDataURL(), toBlob() or captureStream()
Opponent
The old approach relies on bulky third-party libraries that parse DOM nodes and CSS properties one by one to rebuild a facsimile on a canvas: expensive, error-prone and often missing modern CSS layout features (quote: "This approach is computationally expensive, error-prone, and frequently fails to support modern CSS layout features.")
Fallback
Loses the main benefit — Falls back to html2canvas, dom-to-image, snapdom, or rrweb (or unsupported notice), reviving bloat and modern-CSS layout bugs
Unlock
Native rendering paints real DOM subtrees into canvas for pixel-accurate toDataURL(), toBlob(), and captureStream() export

Saving a piece of the page as an image has meant a library re-implementing the browser's layout and painting in JS, and getting it wrong whenever a new CSS feature shows up. The new API has the real engine paint the HTML subtree into a canvas, after which the existing canvas export methods work. Outside Chrome, the fallback is those same libraries, so the opponent stands untouched.

Support HTML-in-Canvas: Limited (Chrome 157+, stable since 2026-11-03; not Firefox or Safari). Since v1.0.1 the guide's fallback section also says "Browser support for HTML-in-canvas: Limited availability. Supported by: Chrome 157 (Nov 2026) and Edge 157 (Nov 2026).", matching this rating

mwg:export-html-media-from-canvas · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Draw real DOM into the canvas so its content is no longer invisible to the browser New capabilityPartialLimited Exposing canvas content to browser features · Canvas content is invisible to the browser
Idea · brainstormText drawn on a canvas (charts, whiteboards, map labels) can be found with Ctrl+F, translated and read by screen readers without maintaining a hidden DOM copy. Chrome 157+ only for now.
Action
Put real HTML children (marked drawable) inside <canvas content="drawable"> and draw them in onpaint with drawElementImage() (or copy them to a texture in WebGL/WebGPU)
Opponent
Content drawn on a regular <canvas> is invisible to screen readers, indexing, translation tools, find-in-page and print (quote: "Regular <canvas> content is not exposed to browser features such as screen readers, indexing, translation tools, accessibility assistive tools, find-in-page, print, etc.")
Fallback
Keeps core behavior — Fall back to overlaying the HTML on the canvas with CSS or a polyfill; the content stays real DOM and only the in-canvas rendering is lost
Unlock
Place real DOM inside <canvas content="drawable"> so rendered content retains screen-reader, translation, search, and print support

A canvas has always been an opaque block of pixels: text on it cannot be selected, searched or translated, and assistive tech cannot read it. The new API keeps the canvas's children laid out and in the DOM tree while the canvas only decides how to paint them; in 2D the browser even aligns hit testing automatically. Cross-origin content cannot be drawn, and with Chrome-only support you have to maintain the fallback alongside it to cover other browsers.

Support HTML-in-Canvas: Limited (Chrome 157+, stable since 2026-11-03; not Firefox or Safari). Since v1.0.1 the guide's fallback section also says "Browser support for HTML-in-canvas: Limited availability. Supported by: Chrome 157 (Nov 2026) and Edge 157 (Nov 2026).", matching this rating

mwg:improve-text-layout-and-legibility:4 · Upstream guide · Line file · v1.0.0

Project real DOM into a 3D scene and hand interaction back to the browser New capabilityPartialLimited Interactive HTML content in 3D scenes · Hand-written interaction inside canvas
Idea · brainstormScreens, boards and control panels inside a 3D scene can be real forms and buttons that accept typing, selection and keyboard focus, with no raycasting-to-event code. Good for product showcases or property panels in a 3D editor. Chrome 157+ only for now.

With the new API a real element sits behind the texture, and the developer only converts the MVP matrix into a canvasTransform each frame to tell the browser where it was drawn. The opponent is described only as "complex": effort, not an observable failure. Matrix syncing is still manual, though Three.js's InteractionManager does it for you.
